### 0.4 Implemented Surface: v0.6.0 Package Staging Script

New file:

    scripts/stage-v0.6.0-package.sh

Script role:

    stage a v0.6.0 rehearsal package from clean tracked repo heads;
    archive the source roots using `git archive HEAD`;
    include carbonstack, carbonstack-comms, and carbonstack-cypher;
    intentionally exclude carbonstack-os;
    write v0.6.0 release rehearsal metadata;
    write checksums and verify them;
    create a tar.gz package archive.

    stage root:
        /tmp/carbonstack-v0.6.0-stage

    package root:

        /tmp/carbonstack-v0.6.0-stage/carbonstack-v0.6.0-package.tar.gz

    requires carbonstack, carbonstack-comms, and carbonstack-cypher repos to exist;
    checks tracked worktree cleanliness for the included repos;
    refuses unsafe stage-root deletion outside `/tmp/carbonstack-*` or `$HOME/carbonstack-*`;
    prints that carbonstack-os is present but intentionally excluded when the OS repo exists.

### 0.10 v0.5.69 Blunders / Continuity Notes

    The first rehearsal attempt failed before staging because the carbonstack worktree was dirty with the new package scripts and registry/table edits. This was correct behavior: the staging script archives HEAD and must not stage uncommitted changes. The workflow was corrected by making a local commit before package rehearsal.

    A terminal paste/glue artifact caused one pre-commit sanity block to be interrupted with ^C and rerun. The rerun succeeded.

    The first full package rehearsal after local commit reached final artifact scan but failed on a false-positive git metadata check. The check used a path fragment `/.git`, which matched tracked `.gitignore` files. This was patched to check actual `.git` files/directories by name with `find . -name ".git"`.

    The local commit was amended from 5e3c6a5 to 7e676cd before push. The bad false-positive scan logic was never pushed.

    The final post-rehearsal marker grep over the `/tmp` rehearsal directory found the script's marker strings rather than a saved rehearsal-output log, because the rehearsal output itself was terminal/stdout, not a file inside the package. This is not a package failure. The terminal log itself contains the successful PACKAGE REHEARSAL PASSED output.

    Large checksum output made the terminal log noisy. This is expected for a package checksum pass and may motivate a future compact checksum summary mode, but it is not a blocker.

    Commit metadata warning repeated again. This remains publishing hygiene, not functional risk.

### 0.7 Implemented Surface: Release Snapshot Hygiene Hardening

Changed file:

    tools/carbonstack-validate/release_snapshot.go

`CheckReleaseSnapshotLayout` now requires these registry artifacts in staged/fresh package roots:

    carbonstack/registry/README.md
    carbonstack/registry/commands.v0.yaml
    carbonstack/registry/COMMAND_BOUNDARY_TABLE.v0.md

Reason:

    G4 command-surface classification is now a hard v0.6.0 gate;
    the command registry and boundary table should not be accidentally absent from a release package;
    release-snapshot should validate that the package contains the classification artifacts needed for public/release claim discipline.

`StrictPreTestArtifactScan` now includes private handoff artifact prefixes:

    CarbonStackLogDoc
    CarbonStack_Breakpoint

Reason:

    Raw private LogDocs and breakpoints are not release-package artifacts;
    prior release scans blocked DBs, sidecar generated state, Rust target output, signer/provider files, OS noise, and executables, but did not explicitly block raw private handoff names;
    sanitized public continuity material remains separate and must be intentionally staged if ever included.

    release_snapshot.go was then patched with a tab-safe line-based approach, adding registry required files and private handoff prefix scanning.

## 0. v0.5.68A Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.68A resolves the explicit v0.5.67 residual caveat.

v0.5.67 successfully introduced the first command boundary table, but it left two malformed package-script entries outside the proper registry entry-list indentation shape:

    carbonstack.script.rehearse-v0.5.0-package
    carbonstack.script.stage-v0.5.0-package

v0.5.68A fixed those entries by normalizing them into the `entries:` list with proper two-space `  - id:` indentation, regenerated the boundary table so it renders 73 entries, and added a format regression test so top-level malformed `- id:` rows fail Go test coverage in the future.

Implemented commit:

    1ca002b registry: fix command boundary table coverage

High-level result:

    no top-level malformed registry IDs remain;
    registry/COMMAND_BOUNDARY_TABLE.v0.md renders 73 registry entries;
    both package-script rows now appear in the command boundary table;
    tools/carbonstack-validate/command_registry_format_test.go prevents the same registry indentation bug from recurring;
    G4 command-surface classification is now clean enough to treat as closed for the v0.6.0 runway, with future enrichment still allowed.

### 0.6 Implemented Surface: Registry Format Regression Test

New file:

    tools/carbonstack-validate/command_registry_format_test.go

New test:

    TestCommandRegistryHasNoTopLevelEntryIDs

Purpose:

    Reads registry/commands.v0.yaml from the runner/test working directory.
    Splits the registry file by line.
    Fails if any line starts with "- id: ".
    Enforces that registry entries remain indented under `entries:` as "  - id: ...".

Why this matters:

    v0.5.67 normal Go registry validation passed even though top-level malformed rows existed, because those rows were invisible to the normal `  - id:` parser.
    This test catches the structural error directly before it can silently disappear from generated/derived registry artifacts again.

### 0.4 Preflight / Failure Discovery

The v0.5.67 scout established that the registry had 64 normal `entries:` rows with core fields present, but Relay/OpenMLS command coverage was incomplete because several Relay/OpenMLS rows were malformed and therefore invisible to simple registry parsing.

Initial patch attempt exposed a real existing defect:

    Relay/OpenMLS command rows already existed in committed HEAD but were malformed:
        - id: comms.openmls-relay-keypackage-submit-dev
        - id: comms.openmls-relay-keypackage-inbox-dev
        - id: comms.openmls-relay-welcome-submit-dev
        - id: comms.openmls-relay-welcome-inbox-dev
        - id: comms.openmls-relay-add-member-dev
        - id: comms.openmls-relay-join-dev
        - id: comms.scripts.openmls-relay-narrow-join-smoke-dev

    The malformed rows used `- id:` at the top level instead of `  - id:` inside the registry entries list.

    The malformed rows also used older/nonstandard field values such as:
        component: comms
        kind: dev-command
        audience: developer
        maturity: experimental

The user correctly stopped after the first table attempt generated only 64 entries and a sanity check mismatch/failure appeared.

Safe cleanup was performed:

    git restore registry/README.md
    rm -f registry/COMMAND_BOUNDARY_TABLE.v0.md

The cleanup returned the worktree to a clean state before registry repair continued.

Added rule:

The rule states:

    Registry entries may include required_flags, optional_flags, and environment metadata when a command/profile/script has important operator-facing inputs.

Added tests:

    TestOpenMLSRelayAddMemberDevDoesNotRunSidecarOrSubmitWelcomeWhenKeyPackageWriteFails
        Sets up a KeyPackage envelope.
        Forces writeRelaySpaceKeyPackageFromEnvelopeForCommand to fail.
        Asserts sidecar add-member is not called.
        Asserts Welcome submit is not called.
        Asserts success output is not printed.

    TestOpenMLSRelayAddMemberDevDoesNotPrintSuccessWhenWelcomeSubmitFails
        Sets up a KeyPackage envelope.
        Allows KeyPackage write to succeed.
        Allows sidecar conversation-add-member to succeed and return a Welcome hint.
        Forces submitRelaySpaceWelcomeEnvelopeForCommand to fail.
        Asserts the sidecar was called first.
        Asserts Welcome submit was attempted.
        Asserts success lines such as status: welcome_created_and_sent, welcome_envelope_id, welcome_delivery_state, keypackage_acked, welcome_acked, member_added, welcome_artifact_written, and group_reloadable are not printed.

Relevant command/function path:

    cmdOpenMLSRelayAddMemberDev
        fetches KeyPackage envelope;
        writes KeyPackage artifact;
        runs sidecar conversation-add-member;
        resolves Welcome artifact path;
        submits Welcome envelope;
        only then prints status: welcome_created_and_sent.

Important callable seams covered by tests:

    relaySpaceOpenMLSArtifactInboxForCommand
    writeRelaySpaceKeyPackageFromEnvelopeForCommand
    runOpenMLSBootstrapSidecarForCommand
    submitRelaySpaceWelcomeEnvelopeForCommand

Behavior changed:

    no runtime behavior changed.

    the failure ordering around add-member is now pinned by tests;

## 0. v0.5.65 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.65 closes the roadmap G3 send/inbox convergence decision after v0.5.63 closed G1 and v0.5.64 closed G2.

The v0.5.65 scout showed that CarbonStack already has consistent OpenMLS dev command names:

    openmls-send-dev
    openmls-inbox-dev

The legacy commands already warn and point users toward those OpenMLS dev commands:

    send   -> warning_replaced_by: openmls-send-dev
    inbox  -> warning_replaced_by: openmls-inbox-dev
    ack    -> legacy delivery/local-processing helper warning

Adding new `message-send-dev` / `message-inbox-dev` aliases would mostly create another naming layer before the release command-boundary table exists. That would increase command-surface drift rather than reduce it.

Therefore v0.5.65 chooses **documented separation**:

    openmls-send-dev and openmls-inbox-dev are the current canonical dev/pre-alpha OpenMLS application-message runtime paths.

    legacy send, inbox, and ack remain legacy/stub-era warning-only continuity surfaces.

    mature product messaging UX remains future work for the early v0.6.x revamp/consolidation arc.

This is a command-surface/release-boundary decision, not a messaging implementation revamp.

### 0.4 Preflight / Scout Findings

The v0.5.65 scout established that a wrapper command is not currently necessary.

Relevant findings:

    command dispatch includes:
        send
        inbox
        ack
        openmls-send-dev
        openmls-inbox-dev
        OpenMLS identity/conversation/relay dev commands

    legacy warnings already point to current OpenMLS dev paths:
        send warning_replaced_by: openmls-send-dev
        inbox warning_replaced_by: openmls-inbox-dev

    openmls-send-dev already:
        requires --to-device, --message, --sidecar-device-label, and --conversation;
        checks local state readiness;
        evaluates trust policy;
        runs sidecar message-protect;
        submits an OpenMLS application-message artifact through Cypher;
        prints command/status/envelope/payload metadata;
        warns that it is dev/pre-alpha and not production messaging UX.

    openmls-inbox-dev already:
        requires --sidecar-device-label and --conversation;
        fetches Cypher inbox envelopes;
        skips unsupported envelopes;
        writes OpenMLS application-message artifacts;
        runs sidecar message-open;
        optionally acks only after sidecar message-open succeeds;
        prints command/status/open/ack metadata;
        warns that it is dev/pre-alpha and not production messaging UX.

    existing tests cover meaningful runtime boundaries:
        send rejects missing required flags;
        send does not submit if sidecar protect fails;
        send submits application-message artifact after protect succeeds;
        inbox rejects missing required flags;
        inbox skips unsupported envelopes;
        inbox does not ack when message-open fails;
        inbox acks only after message-open succeeds.

Conclusion:

    Do not add new wrapper/alias commands now.
    Declare existing OpenMLS dev commands canonical for v0.6.0 dev/pre-alpha runtime messaging.
    Preserve legacy warnings and explicit nonclaims.
    Defer mature product messaging UX and deeper command consolidation to early v0.6.x.

## 0. v0.5.64 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.64 implements the roadmap G2 decision after v0.5.63 closed G1.

v0.5.63 established a non-encrypting state path contract and proved that state-domain path resolution agrees with existing trust/candidate path derivation. v0.5.64 uses that contract in a deliberately narrow runtime seam:

    app.resolveCommandStatePaths(statePath)
        resolves comms_state, trust_store, trust_history, and candidate_store through state.ResolveStateDomainPath;
        returns a compact commandStatePaths bundle;
        exposes trust.Paths-compatible paths to existing command code;
        does not read/write/delete/encrypt state.

The patch replaces selected command-side direct calls to:

    trust.PathsForStatePath(*statePath)

with:

    commandPaths, err := resolveCommandStatePaths(*statePath)
    paths := commandPaths.TrustPaths

This is **read-only path resolution only**. It is not a vault-security change and not a broad state-loader rewrite.

Current public Gitea-source-of-truth release remains:

    v0.5.0 Runtime and Registry Validation Minor Epoch Pre-Release

v0.5.64 is mainline development state, not a new public release package.

Behavior:

    uses state.StateAuditOptions{StatePath: statePath};
    resolves StateDomainCommsState through state.ResolveStateDomainPath;

    does not create files;

    does not encrypt or claim vault security.

## 0. v0.5.63 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.63 is the first **contract** rung after the v0.5.62 state-domain/vault-adapter skeleton.

The v0.5.62 skeleton gave CarbonStack a typed domain map and a non-encrypting `LocalPathVaultAdapter`. The v0.5.63 scout showed that command state handling is still widely distributed across `internal/app/commands.go`, `internal/app/openmls_runtime.go`, and `internal/app/openmls_relay_dev.go`, with many `--state` flags and direct calls into `state.Require`, `state.RequireReadyDevice`, `state.Save`, `state.ServerFromStateOrFlag`, and `trust.PathsForStatePath`.

Because of that, v0.5.63 intentionally does **not** wire commands through the adapter yet. Instead, it lands a narrower and safer contract layer:

    StatePathContractSchemaVersion
    StatePathContract
    StatePathContractDomain
    StatePathContractCapabilities
    BuildStatePathContract
    ResolveStateDomainPath

The purpose is to prove that the domain resolver is a stable, machine-readable, non-mutating path contract before any runtime command behavior is changed.

### 0.2 Current Public Release

Current public Gitea-source-of-truth release remains:

    v0.5.0 Runtime and Registry Validation Minor Epoch Pre-Release

v0.5.63 is mainline development state, not a new public release package.

It does not retag v0.5.0 and does not create new release assets.

### 0.4 Preflight / Scout Findings

The v0.5.63 preflight established why this rung needed to be contract-only.

Key findings:

    state package owns:
        DefaultStatePath
        Load
        Require
        RequireReadyDevice
        Save
        ServerFromStateOrFlag

    command surfaces own many direct --state flags and direct state calls:
        state.Save
        state.Require
        state.RequireReadyDevice
        state.ServerFromStateOrFlag
        trust.PathsForStatePath

    OpenMLS dev surfaces also own direct --state flags:
        openmls-send-dev
        openmls-inbox-dev
        Relay Space KeyPackage / Welcome / add-member / join dev commands

    trust package has its own path derivation:
        PathsForStatePath
        IdentityCandidatesPathForStatePath

    state-domain registry independently resolves the same trust/candidate paths:
        trust.json
        trust-events.jsonl
        identity-candidates.json

Conclusion:

    Do not wire commands yet.
    Do not change state.Save yet.
    Do not move runtime state behavior behind the adapter yet.
    First prove that the state-domain contract and existing trust path helpers agree.

### 0.6 Tests Added

Added in `internal/state/path_contract_test.go`:

    TestBuildStatePathContractIsNonEncryptingAndNonMutating
        Confirms schema version and state path.
        Confirms domains exist.
        Confirms encryption/read/write/delete capabilities are false.
        Confirms building the contract does not create state.json or trust.json.

    TestStatePathContractResolvesExpectedLocalDomains
        Confirms comms_state resolves to the given state path.

        Confirms unknown domains return an error.

## 0. v0.5.62 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.62 is a combined implementation checkpoint with two related outcomes:

    v0.5.62-A:
        Legacy `send`, `inbox`, and `ack` now emit explicit warning lines before continuing through their old behavior.

    v0.5.62-B:
        State-domain and vault-adjacent knowledge was factored out of the audit function into typed domain definitions and a non-encrypting local-path vault adapter skeleton.

This rung keeps implementation momentum without overclaiming maturity.

The legacy command change does not remove, reject, or replace the old commands yet. It makes their current status visible at runtime:

    send:
        legacy/stub-era send path;
        uses mock/stub message encryption;
        not mature OpenMLS-backed send UX;
        points to openmls-send-dev.

    inbox:
        legacy/stub-era inbox path;
        may print stub_plaintext;
        not mature OpenMLS-backed inbox UX;
        points to openmls-inbox-dev.

    ack:
        legacy ack helper;
        not a standalone secure receive proof;
        not trust, identity verification, hostile-server safety, or production security.

The vault skeleton does not encrypt or store secrets. It only gives code a typed model for the domains already surfaced by `state-audit-dev`.

    StateDomainCommsState
    StateDomainTrustStore
    StateDomainTrustHistory
    StateDomainCandidateStore
    StateDomainSidecarGeneratedState
    StateDomainSidecarBuildOutput
    StateDomainLocalCypherDB

New vault class taxonomy:

    local_app_state
    local_trust_state
    append_only_trust_history
    trust_adjacent_candidate_state
    generated_secret_state
    generated_build_output
    server_relay_local_state

New domain types/functions:

    type StateDomainID
    type VaultClass
    type StateDomainDefinition
    type StateDomainResolution
    ResolveDefaultStateDomains(opts StateAuditOptions) []StateDomainResolution

New adapter skeleton:

    type VaultAdapter interface
    type LocalPathVaultAdapter
    NewLocalPathVaultAdapter(opts StateAuditOptions) LocalPathVaultAdapter

Adapter capabilities intentionally return false:

    EncryptionEnabled() == false
    CanReadSecretContents() == false
    CanWriteSecretContents() == false
    CanDeleteDomains() == false

Adapter behavior:

    ListDomains() returns a copy of the resolved domain slice.
    Resolve(domainID) returns a path/domain resolution or an unknown-domain error.
    It only resolves local paths and metadata.
    It does not read secret contents.
    It does not write secret contents.
    It does not delete domains.
    It does not encrypt anything.

`state-audit-dev` integration:

    state.AuditStateDomains now consumes NewLocalPathVaultAdapter(opts).ListDomains().
    StateAuditDomain now includes:
        vault_class
    Text output now prints:
        vault_class: ...
    JSON output now includes:
        "vault_class": "..."

## 0. v0.5.61 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.61 is the state-audit hardening rung immediately after the v0.5.60 implementation pivot.

v0.5.60 created `state-audit-dev`, the first executable state/vault-spine primitive. v0.5.61 makes that primitive useful as a future tooling boundary by adding machine-readable JSON output.

Consensus entering v0.5.61:

    state-audit hardening comes first;
    legacy send/inbox should receive warnings soon, but not rejection/removal yet;
    machine-readable output is needed;
    vault path/domain abstraction and later encrypted-store work can follow in sequence.

v0.5.61 therefore implements:

    state-audit-dev --format text
    state-audit-dev --format json

The JSON format exposes the same non-mutating state-domain classification as structured data and includes:

    schema_version;
    command;
    mutation_allowed;
    raw_secret_contents_printed;
    domains_total;
    domains_present;
    domains_absent;
    domains[];
    warning.

This is the first stable-ish contract that later vault/domain tooling can consume.

    marks secret-bearing / maybe-secret / non-secret boundaries;
    marks future-vault-required boundaries;
    marks safe-to-print-content false for all audited domains;
    marks mutation_allowed false;
    does not read or print raw secret contents;
    does not mutate trust.json;
    does not mutate trust-events.jsonl;
    does not mutate identity-candidates.json;
    does not delete cypher.db;
    does not delete sidecar state;
    does not delete build output.

Initial audited domains:

    comms_state
        default path: .carbonstack-comms/state.json
        classification: local-app-state
        future vault required: true

    trust_store
        default path: .carbonstack-comms/trust.json
        classification: local-trust-state
        future vault required: true

    trust_history
        default path: .carbonstack-comms/trust-events.jsonl
        classification: append-only-trust-history
        future vault required: true

    candidate_store
        default path: .carbonstack-comms/identity-candidates.json
        classification: local-trust-adjacent-candidate-state
        future vault required: true

    sidecar_generated_state
        default path: internal/protocol/mls/openmls-sidecar/.carbonstack-openmls-sidecar-state
        classification: generated-dev-provider-state
        future vault required: true
        secret-bearing: yes

    sidecar_build_output
        default path: internal/protocol/mls/openmls-sidecar/target
        classification: generated-build-output
        future vault required: false

    local_cypher_db
        default path: ../carbonstack-cypher/cypher.db
        classification: server-relay-local-db
        future vault required: false for Comms vault, but may contain relay metadata/envelopes and must not be dumped casually.

Boundary:

    `state-audit-dev` is dev/pre-alpha.
    It is an inventory/introspection helper.
    It is not vault encryption.
    It is not recovery.
    It is not deletion or cleanup.
    It is not production key storage.
    It is not trust verification.
    It is not identity verification.

    The assistant previously over-optimized Go version minimization. The useful result was discovering that Go 1.24 cannot satisfy current `modernc.org/sqlite`; the recovery was to restore the previously validating `go 1.26.3` module floor and move on.

### 0.11 Recommended Next Work

Recommended next rung: **v0.5.61 send/inbox semantics implementation pivot.**

Why:

    The recon repeatedly showed mature send/inbox UX remains a major functional gap.
    Legacy `send`/`inbox` still exist and remain stub-era.
    OpenMLS send/inbox dev surfaces exist but are separate command islands.
    Relay Space KeyPackage/Welcome inbox paths exist but are artifact-specific.
    v0.5.60 now gives a state/vault spine primitive, so the next functional gap is user-facing receive/send semantics.

Recommended v0.5.61 options, in priority order:

    Option A: implement loud legacy send/inbox guardrails.
        Make legacy `send`/`inbox` output unmistakably stub-era and point to OpenMLS dev surfaces.
        Low risk; reduces UX confusion.

    Option B: implement a unified dev inbox/read command wrapper.
        A dev-only receive surface that clearly chooses one safe current path or refuses ambiguous state.
        Higher value, higher seam risk.

    Option C: expand state-audit-dev into JSON output / machine-readable audit.
        Useful for vault, but less functional than send/inbox UX.

    Option D: begin vault adapter abstraction.
        Too early for encryption, but a domain-aware interface could be planned after send/inbox semantics are less fragmented.

Recommended default:

    v0.5.61 should start with a targeted scout for `send`, `inbox`, `openmls-send-dev`, `openmls-inbox-dev`, Relay Space KeyPackage/Welcome inbox commands, and command output semantics.
    Then implement either Option A or B depending on seam cleanliness.

## 0. v0.5.58-REFACTOR Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.58-REFACTOR is a planning/refactor overlay after the v0.5.58 add-member sidecar-failure test.

The user raised a scope-drift concern: implementation appeared to be moving quickly, while the public-surface CLI, README/roadmap truth, key storage status, and inbox semantics were not obviously reconciled.

A repo/logdoc/roadmap review found the concern valid:

    implementation is not nonsense drift;
    failure-path work improved layer separation;
    but release-surface truth drift is now the main risk;
    the roadmap/docs index/README surfaces are behind actual mainline state;
    the public CLI/manual boundary is not a clean milestone yet;
    key storage/vault is not complete;
    inbox semantics are fragmented across stub-era and dev OpenMLS paths;
    repo-local generated artifact/toolchain hygiene should be resolved before v0.6.0 prep.

Decision:

    collapse the next priorities into a large, documented cleanup/refactor rung;
    make surface READMEs evergreen;
    refactor roadmap/logdoc priorities before more feature work;
    delay repo-local cypher.db cleanup to the pre-release hygiene rung;
    keep relay-openmls-join-dev out of full/release-snapshot until a deliberate v0.6.0 decision.

This is still not local-backbone.

This is still not production secure messaging.

This is still not identity verification.

This is still not hostile-server safety.

This is still not metadata privacy.

### 0.2 Current Repo Heads

No repo changes were made by this REFACTOR artifact itself. It records the state after v0.5.58:

    carbonstack        39e2c23 docs: map Relay OpenMLS negative-path hardening
    carbonstack-comms  a72b23d test: cover Relay OpenMLS add-member sidecar failure
    carbonstack-cypher 59b74c9 docs: define local Cypher validation state contract
    carbonstack-os     1bbbe52 docs: clarify CarbonStackOS target direction

### 0.3 New / Updated Planning Artifacts

Generated handoff artifacts:

    CarbonStack_Long_Term_Roadmap_v0.5.58_REFACTOR.pdf
    CarbonStack_Long_Term_Roadmap_v0.5.58_REFACTOR.md
    CarbonStackLogDocV0.5.58_REFACTOR.md
    CarbonStack_BreakpointV0.5.58_REFACTOR.json

These are planning artifacts. They are not repo commits and not public release assets until manually reviewed and committed/uploaded.

### 0.4 Scope-Drift Findings

#### Public roadmap/docs surface drift

The v0.5.48 roadmap was directionally useful but stale after v0.5.52-v0.5.58. The repo roadmap surface also lagged behind current reality. The current public-facing docs should not require a reader to infer current state from a stack of old docs.

#### Public CLI/manual surface gap

The project has a command registry and many dev command surfaces, but it lacks a clean public CLI/manual boundary:

    public/release-facing commands;
    dev-only commands;
    hidden/private validation commands;
    historical commands;
    unsafe/not-for-public-copy-paste commands;
    v0.6.0 candidate commands.

This should become a first-class cleanup target before v0.6.0.

#### Key storage/vault is not complete

The project has useful state inventory, storage domain modeling, trust/candidate/recovery helpers, and dev OpenMLS state boundaries. It does not have production vault/key storage, authenticated local state, mature backup/restore, re-enrollment, or no-silent-regeneration enforcement everywhere.

#### Inbox semantics are fragmented

Current inbox-like paths include:

    old stub-era comms inbox;
    OpenMLS application-message dev inbox;
    Relay Space KeyPackage inbox/write;
    Relay Space Welcome inbox/write;
    join command with optional Welcome ack after join success.

These are useful dev surfaces, not one mature public inbox semantics model.

#### Stub-era send/inbox must remain loudly labeled

Existing `send` / `inbox` remain stub-era and must not be mistaken for the mature OpenMLS/Relay Space user path.

#### Hygiene and toolchain truth remain pre-release items

Repo-local generated artifact review, especially `carbonstack-cypher/cypher.db`, should be handled during pre-release repo hygiene. Go/Rust/SQLite toolchain requirements should be reconciled before package rehearsal.

### 0.5 Refactored Priority Decision

The next priority is no longer “keep adding small failure tests until exhaustion.”

Refactored next priority:

    large documented cleanup/refactor rung;
    evergreen README pass;
    docs index and roadmap current-state pass;
    CLI/manual/registry boundary plan;
    send/inbox semantics audit;
    key storage/vault current-state audit;
    artifact/toolchain hygiene;
    then decide whether remaining add-member edge tests or v0.6.0 release prep should resume.

### 0.6 Large Cleaning Rung Definition

The cleaning rung should include:

    1. Surface README evergreen pass across carbonstack, carbonstack-comms, carbonstack-cypher, carbonstack-os.
    2. Docs index update that treats docs as an archive and points to current known-good docs.
    3. Roadmap update from v0.5.48/v0.5.58 reality.
    4. Registry/CLI/manual categorization.
    5. Stub send/inbox vs dev OpenMLS command distinction.
    6. Key storage/vault not-complete statement.
    7. Inbox semantics not-mature/unified statement.
    8. relay-openmls-join-dev release-inclusion criteria.
    9. Repo-local generated artifact cleanup policy.
    10. Toolchain truth check.
    11. Public-claim audit before v0.6.0.

### 0.7 Proposed Rung Refactor

Recommended next ladder:

    v0.5.59-REFACTOR:
        Commit roadmap/logdoc refactor and create cleanup execution plan.

    v0.5.60:
        Evergreen README pass across public surfaces.

    v0.5.61:
        Docs index + repo roadmap current-state update.

    v0.5.62:
        CLI/manual/registry boundary plan and/or generated command-reference design.

    v0.5.63:
        Toolchain + artifact hygiene checkpoint, including repo-local cypher.db decision.

    v0.5.64:
        Decide whether to resume remaining add-member edge tests or move into v0.6.0 validation-profile inclusion decision.

    pre-v0.6.0:
        Release-surface claim audit, package rehearsal, and deliberate release-snapshot/full inclusion decisions.

Version numbers are flexible; the important change is priority order.

### 0.8 Blunders / Recovery Notes

    The user's scope-drift gut feeling was valid. It did not indicate recent tests were wrong; it indicated public/release surface truth was falling behind implementation.
    The v0.5.48 roadmap remained directionally useful but was stale after v0.5.52-v0.5.58.
    The project lacked a clean current public CLI/manual milestone despite having a registry and many dev commands.
    Key storage/vault and inbox semantics were easy to mentally over-assume because adjacent helper/scaffold work exists; this REFACTOR explicitly marks them not complete.
    Repo-local artifact hygiene should not be mixed into tiny feature-test rungs; it belongs in a documented pre-release hygiene rung.
    Surface READMEs should become evergreen to avoid repeatedly rotting with version-specific claims.
    This REFACTOR is intentionally not a code patch and not a release package.

### 0.9 Do Not Do Next

Do not:

    continue small failure tests indefinitely without cleanup;
    claim key storage/vault complete;
    claim inbox semantics unified/mature;
    make relay-openmls-join-dev public/release-facing by accident;
    add relay-openmls-join-dev to full/release-snapshot without a v0.6.0 decision;
    promote dev commands into public CLI docs without categorization;
    leave surface READMEs with stale version-specific current-state claims;
    delete repo-local generated artifacts without an explicit hygiene decision;
    treat roadmap/logdoc refactor as code evidence;
    claim local-backbone, production security, hostile-server safety, metadata privacy, verified identity, vault readiness, or PQ/hybrid readiness.

### 0.10 Immediate Next Action

Start the cleanup/refactor execution arc:

    1. Review and, if acceptable, commit/reference the REFACTOR roadmap/logdoc artifacts.
    2. Begin evergreen README pass across public surfaces.
    3. Update docs index and roadmap current-state surfaces.
    4. Define CLI/manual/registry command categories.
    5. Then decide whether to resume remaining add-member edge tests or proceed toward v0.6.0 validation-profile/release-surface planning.

## 0. v0.5.58 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.58 is a targeted Comms command-test hardening rung.

v0.5.57 found that the originally suspected join/ACK_AFTER_JOIN failure cases were already covered:

    no ack by default;
    ACK_AFTER_JOIN success after join;
    no ack when sidecar conversation-join fails;
    no ack when Welcome write fails;
    rejection when no Welcome envelope exists.

v0.5.57 also found that Cypher ack/routing negative coverage and runner helper negative coverage were already strong.

The remaining useful implementation target was add-member / KeyPackage-to-Welcome failure ordering.

v0.5.58 implements the first narrow test for that target:

    TestOpenMLSRelayAddMemberDevDoesNotSubmitWelcomeWhenSidecarAddMemberFails

This test proves the command returns the sidecar error, does not call the Welcome submit helper, and does not print success-related output when `conversation-add-member` fails.

This is still not local-backbone.

This is still not production secure messaging.

This is still not identity verification.

This is still not hostile-server safety.

This is still not metadata privacy.

### 0.2 Current Repo Heads

After v0.5.58 patching, validation, commit, push, and final snapshot:

    carbonstack        39e2c23 docs: map Relay OpenMLS negative-path hardening
    carbonstack-comms  a72b23d test: cover Relay OpenMLS add-member sidecar failure
    carbonstack-cypher 59b74c9 docs: define local Cypher validation state contract
    carbonstack-os     1bbbe52 docs: clarify CarbonStackOS target direction

Final snapshot showed all four repos clean/aligned with origin/main.

### 0.3 Changed Surfaces

`carbonstack-comms` changed:

    internal/app/openmls_relay_dev_test.go
      Added:
          TestOpenMLSRelayAddMemberDevDoesNotSubmitWelcomeWhenSidecarAddMemberFails

No `carbonstack`, `carbonstack-cypher`, `carbonstack-os`, runner code, Comms runtime code, Cypher routes/schema, sidecar code, registry metadata, or front README changes occurred in this rung.

### 0.4 New Test Behavior

The new test uses existing command test seams:

    relaySpaceOpenMLSArtifactInboxForCommand
    writeRelaySpaceKeyPackageFromEnvelopeForCommand
    runOpenMLSBootstrapSidecarForCommand
    submitRelaySpaceWelcomeEnvelopeForCommand

The test simulates:

    a valid queued KeyPackage envelope;
    successful KeyPackage artifact write;
    sidecar command invoked as conversation-add-member;
    sidecar returning error:
        sidecar add-member failed

The test asserts:

    `cmdOpenMLSRelayAddMemberDev` returns an error containing:
        sidecar add-member failed

    the sidecar command actually reached:
        conversation-add-member

    `submitRelaySpaceWelcomeEnvelopeForCommand` is not called;

    captured output does not include success-only fields:
        status: welcome_created_and_sent
        welcome_envelope_id:
        welcome_delivery_state:
        keypackage_acked: false
        welcome_acked: false

This preserves the important failure ordering:

    KeyPackage retrieval/write may occur;
    sidecar add-member failure stops the command;
    no Welcome is submitted after sidecar failure;
    no misleading success output is printed;
    no ack behavior is introduced.

### 0.8 Relationship to Protected Ack Rule

v0.5.58 does not add an add-member ack path.

The protected rules remain:

    KeyPackage is not acked by add-member;
    Welcome is not acked by add-member;
    Welcome ack is controlled by the later join command and only after successful sidecar conversation-join when explicitly requested;
    ack remains local-processing / delivery state, not trust, verification, identity acceptance, or security certification.

The new test strengthens the adjacent invariant:

    if add-member fails at sidecar stage, the command never reaches Welcome submit and never prints success fields.

## 0. v0.5.57 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.57 is a docs/update breakpoint for Comms-side Relay OpenMLS no-ack/failure coverage.

The starting assumption after v0.5.56 was that the first useful live/focused failure-path target would likely be:

    openmls-relay-join-dev sidecar conversation-join failure;
    prove ACK_AFTER_JOIN does not ack when join fails;
    or prove ACK_AFTER_JOIN does not ack when Welcome retrieval/write fails.

Recon showed that this was already materially covered.

Therefore v0.5.57 did not implement a new test.

Instead it records the coverage map and gap diagnosis:

    join / Welcome / ACK_AFTER_JOIN coverage is already strong at the Comms command-test layer;
    Cypher Relay Space/wrong-recipient/wrong-space ack coverage is already strong at the Cypher HTTP/API test layer;
    runner negative helper coverage is already strong after v0.5.55;
    add-member / KeyPackage-to-Welcome failure behavior is the next best implementation target;
    repo-local carbonstack-cypher/cypher.db remains a separate hygiene/release-readiness item.

This is still not local-backbone.

This is still not production secure messaging.

This is still not identity verification.

This is still not hostile-server safety.

This is still not metadata privacy.

### 0.9 Protected Ack Rule

The coverage note explicitly records the protected ack rule:

    Welcome ack is optional.
    Welcome is not acked by default.
    Welcome may be acked only when ACK_AFTER_JOIN / --ack-after-join is explicitly requested.
    Welcome ack may occur only after sidecar conversation-join succeeds.
    Ack is local-processing / delivery state, not identity verification or trust.

Also preserved:

    KeyPackage is not acked by the narrow join smoke script.
    Add-member does not ack the KeyPackage.
    Add-member does not ack the Welcome.

### 0.5 v0.5.56 Recon / Decision Context

The preflight question was whether to start implementing live negative-path behavior immediately.

Candidate negatives included:

    wrong recipient ack;
    wrong Relay Space ack;
    no ack on sidecar join failure;
    no ack on add-member failure;
    stale sidecar refusal;
    repo-local cypher.db hygiene.

Recon result:

    wrong Relay Space ack and wrong recipient ack are already materially covered at the Cypher HTTP/API test layer;
    v0.5.55 already covers runner-local DB/assertion negative behavior;
    relay-openmls-join-dev remains healthy as positive-path proof;
    the remaining high-value gaps are mostly Comms/OpenMLS failure paths around sidecar add-member failure, sidecar join failure, Welcome write failure, and ensuring ACK_AFTER_JOIN does not ack when the relevant write/join step fails.

Decision:

    write a design matrix first;
    avoid duplicating existing Cypher API coverage inside the long runner profile;
    keep relay-openmls-join-dev positive-path;
    prefer targeted Comms tests or small dev harnesses for next failure-path work;
    defer repo-local cypher.db deletion/cleanup to a separate explicit hygiene rung.

### 0.6 Coverage Map Recorded

The design matrix records four coverage groups.

#### 0.6.1 Cypher-owned coverage

Already materially covered at Cypher HTTP/API layer:

    scoped submit returns relay_space_id and queued state;
    scoped inbox returns only matching Relay Space envelopes;
    scoped ack returns relay_space_id and acknowledged state;
    scoped inbox becomes empty after scoped ack;
    wrong Relay Space ack rejects with envelope_not_found;
    wrong recipient ack rejects with recipient_mismatch;
    missing Relay Space scoped submit/inbox rejects.

Interpretation:

    wrong Relay Space ack and wrong recipient ack do not need immediate duplication inside relay-openmls-join-dev.

They may be re-surfaced later in a small runner-facing negative profile if release-readiness requires runner-level proof.

#### 0.6.2 Runner-owned helper coverage

Already covered by v0.5.55:

    missing KeyPackage delivery state is refused during compact result collection;
    missing Welcome delivery state is refused during compact result collection;
    DB assertion fails on missing Welcome;
    DB assertion fails on unexpected ack in no-ack mode;
    DB assertion fails on missing ack in ACK_AFTER_JOIN mode;
    DB assertion fails on queued Welcome in ACK_AFTER_JOIN mode;
    DB assertion fails on missing KeyPackage;
    trust/candidate file presence fails absence checks;
    count mismatch fails as expected.

Interpretation:

    the runner can detect bad post-run DB/result states, but this is not the same as live failure-path exercise.

#### 0.6.3 Positive-path profile coverage

`relay-openmls-join-dev` currently covers:

    no-ack KeyPackage -> add-member -> Welcome -> join;
    ACK_AFTER_JOIN KeyPackage -> add-member -> Welcome -> join -> scoped Welcome ack;
    fresh runner-owned temp roots;
    dynamic local Cypher ports;
    unique sidecar labels;
    stale sidecar-device refusal before profile run;
    trust/candidate absence checks before and after;
    exact DB assertions for no-ack and ACK_AFTER_JOIN.

Interpretation:

    this is strong positive-path validation, not hostile-server validation or broad failure-path proof.

#### 0.6.4 Artifact/hygiene coverage

Current artifact-scan review hit remains:

    carbonstack-cypher/cypher.db

Interpretation:

    the repo-local DB is not used by relay-openmls-join-dev, which uses runner-owned temp DBs;
    it remains a hygiene/release-readiness item;
    it should not be silently deleted as part of negative-path work.

### 0.7 Remaining Negative / Failure-Path Gaps

Comms-owned gaps remain the most important next implementation candidates:

    no KeyPackage envelope;
    no Welcome envelope;
    sidecar conversation-add-member failure;
    sidecar conversation-join failure;
    Welcome write failure;
    proof no ack on Welcome write failure;
    proof no ack on sidecar join failure;
    ack client failure after successful join.

The design matrix recommends implementing these as targeted Comms tests or small dev harnesses, not by bloating `relay-openmls-join-dev`.

Potential later Cypher/runner coverage:

    a small runner-facing `relay-space-ack-negative-dev` profile may be useful later if release/public evidence needs runner-level proof of wrong Relay Space / wrong recipient ack rejection.

But this is not the next default move because Cypher API tests already cover those cases at the right layer.

### 0.8 Recommended Next Implementation Order

The new design matrix recommends:

    v0.5.57:
        targeted Comms no-ack-on-failure test planning/recon.
        Prefer unit/focused tests around openmls-relay-join-dev and ack-after-join behavior.

    v0.5.58:
        implement first cheap Comms failure-path test if recon is clean:
            no ack when sidecar conversation-join fails; or
            missing Welcome behavior; or
            no ack when Welcome retrieval/write fails.

    v0.5.59:
        targeted add-member failure-path test:
            no Welcome ack;
            no KeyPackage ack;
            no trust/candidate mutation;
            clear command failure output.

    v0.5.60:
        artifact hygiene / release-readiness checkpoint:
            decide on repo-local carbonstack-cypher/cypher.db;
            confirm profile remains out of full/release-snapshot;
            confirm registry/front README boundaries.

Alternative:

    v0.5.57 may be a hygiene rung first if repo-local DB or generated roots become release-snapshot blockers.

### 0.9 Placement Rule Established

v0.5.56 establishes the placement rule:

    Do not put every negative case into relay-openmls-join-dev.

Preferred placement:

    Cypher HTTP/API tests for routing/ack authorization;
    Comms command tests for sidecar/write/join/ack failure behavior;
    runner helper tests for DB/assertion/output behavior;
    separate runner negative profile only when live runner evidence is specifically valuable.

This keeps the long runner profile from becoming a brittle mega-harness.

### 0.4 Validation / Profile Run / Commit / Push

Initial negative-helper test attempt failed before the final patch.

The failure was useful and exposed two test/logic details:

    assertRelayOpenMLSDBState checks total envelope count before content-specific KeyPackage/Welcome counts. Therefore missing-Welcome and missing-KeyPackage fixtures with only one envelope failed first with:
        envelopes count = 1, want 2

    relayOpenMLSSQLiteScalar returns an empty string without error when a scalar query finds zero rows. Therefore collectRelayOpenMLSSubrunResult originally did not fail when the Welcome row was missing.

Recovery patch:

    added explicit empty-string checks for KeyPackage and Welcome delivery-state scalars;
    adjusted missing-artifact fixtures to include a filler envelope so total envelope count remains 2 and content-specific assertions are exercised;
    updated the missing-Welcome result-collection negative test to expect:
        missing Welcome delivery state in profile DB

### 0.5 v0.5.53 Recon / Decision Context

v0.5.53 started as profile-hardening / evidence-retention / hygiene preflight after v0.5.52.

Recon showed:

    relay-openmls-join-dev already passes;
    runner-owned temp root is removed after profile completion;
    detailed smoke logs and temp DBs therefore disappear unless the console log is captured;
    retaining generated files could create source hygiene ambiguity;
    a compact console summary is lower-risk than retained evidence files;
    registry already had the profile entry but did not mention --compact-summary after the first compact-summary patch;
    registry flags should not become separate top-level entries by default, but material flags should be documented inside affected command/profile entries;
    --compact-summary changes the evidence presentation and should be documented as an optional flag for runner.relay-openmls-join-dev.

Decision after recon:

    implement compact console summary only;
    do not retain generated evidence files;
    update registry entry in-place after confirming flag belongs in the private registry metadata;
    do not create a standalone registry entry for --compact-summary.

Rejected/deferred for this rung:

    retained evidence directory/file output;
    negative-path hardening;
    failure-path profile checks;
    public README promotion;
    adding relay-openmls-join-dev to full or release-snapshot;
    Comms/Cypher code changes;
    trust/candidate mutation;
    local-backbone claims.

### 0.7 Registry / Flag Doctrine Established

v0.5.53 clarified registry doctrine for runner flags:

    profiles/scripts/commands get registry entries;
    flags do not normally get their own registry entries;
    flags should be documented inside affected entries when they materially change behavior, evidence shape, cleanup, safety, or claim boundaries.

For this exact case:

    --compact-summary is not a separate command surface;
    --compact-summary is a material evidence/output flag;
    it belongs inside the hidden/private runner.relay-openmls-join-dev registry entry as an optional flag;
    it should not be promoted to front README;
    it should not preserve generated artifacts;
    it should not change validation scope.

Registry entry now records:

    example:
        cd carbonstack/tools/carbonstack-validate && go run . --profile relay-openmls-join-dev --compact-summary

    optional_flags:
        --compact-summary
            meaning: Print a compact evidence summary after successful profile execution.
            boundary: Output/evidence convenience only; does not preserve generated artifacts or change validation scope.

    nonclaims:
        not local-backbone;
        not production secure messaging;
        not identity verification;
        not hostile-server safety;
        not metadata privacy;
        not audit or certification.

This keeps the registry honest without turning it into a full manpage.

    runner runs an ACK_AFTER_JOIN narrow smoke subrun in a separate fresh subrun;
    runner asserts output and DB state for both subruns;
    runner checks expected trust/candidate files are absent before/after;
    runner removes its runner-owned temp root after completion.

This is the first repeatable runner-backed proof of the v0.5.49/v0.5.50 manual smoke evidence pair.

### 0.6 Profile Contract Actually Implemented

The implemented profile follows the v0.5.51 design contract closely.

Implemented generated-state behavior:

    creates a runner-owned temp root:
        /tmp/carbonstack-relay-openmls-join-dev-<random>

    builds a temporary Cypher binary:
        <temp_root>/carbonstack-cypher-relay-openmls

    creates separate subrun temp directories:
        <temp_root>/no-ack
        <temp_root>/ack-after-join

    creates per-subrun Cypher DBs:
        <subrun>/cypher.db

    creates per-subrun Comms states:
        <subrun>/alice-state.json
        <subrun>/bob-state.json

    creates unique sidecar labels derived from a run ID:
        carbonstack-v0552...-noack-alice-device
        carbonstack-v0552...-noack-bob-device
        carbonstack-v0552...-ack-alice-device
        carbonstack-v0552...-ack-bob-device

    creates unique conversation labels derived from the same run ID.

Implemented cleanup behavior:

    removes the runner-owned temp root after profile completion;
    does not remove unknown sidecar state;
    does not remove unknown provider storage;
    does not remove user trust/candidate files;
    does not remove repo docs/source.

Implemented refusal behavior:

    refuses if the generated sidecar device label path already exists;
    uses unique labels so collision is unlikely;
    still leaves broader stale-state/failure-path hardening as future work.

Implemented profile surface:

    profile claims positive-path local/dev validation only;
    output prints nonclaims up front;
    registry entry remains include_in_front_readme: false.

### 0.6 Future Profile Claim Contract

Preferred future profile name:

    relay-openmls-join-dev

Maximum allowed future profile claim:

    In a fresh runner-owned local/dev environment, CarbonStack can start a local Cypher dev server, create isolated Alice/Bob Comms/Cypher/Relay Space state, create isolated OpenMLS sidecar state, run the KeyPackage -> add-member -> Welcome -> join path, prove no-ack and ACK_AFTER_JOIN behavior, and confirm checked trust/candidate stores are not created or mutated by that path.

Additional allowed future claims:

    package tests passed for involved repos;
    Cypher health responded;
    Relay Space scoped envelopes behaved as expected;
    Welcome ack occurred only after join success when explicitly requested.

The future profile must not claim:

    local-backbone;
    production secure messaging;
    hostile-server safety;
    metadata privacy;
    verified identity;
    secure enrollment;
    mature provider live-flow;
    public CLI readiness;
    deployment readiness;
    audit;
    certification;
    general-public usability;
    trust-store correctness;
    candidate-store correctness;
    key-compromise recovery correctness;
    vault security;
    PQ/hybrid security.

### 0.7 Generated-State and Cleanup Contract

Future profile-generated state should live under a runner-owned temp root, for example:

    /tmp/carbonstack-validate-relay-openmls-join-dev-<random>/

Profile-owned generated state may include:

    cypher/cypher.db;
    cypher/cypher.log;
    comms/alice-state.json;
    comms/bob-state.json;
    smoke/no-ack.log;
    smoke/ack-after-join.log;
    evidence/db-summary.txt;
    evidence/trust-candidate-before.txt;
    evidence/trust-candidate-after.txt.

Since current sidecar behavior uses repo-local `.carbonstack-openmls-sidecar-state`, the first implementation should use unique sidecar labels and refuse to proceed if those labels already exist.

Future generated labels should be unique per run, such as:

    carbonstack-v0552-<random>-alice-device;
    carbonstack-v0552-<random>-bob-device;
    carbonstack-v0552-<random>-conversation;
    relay-openmls-join-dev-<random>;
    relay-openmls-join-dev-alice-<random>;
    relay-openmls-join-dev-bob-<random>.

First implementation should prefer safe refusal over destructive cleanup.

Required refusal cases:

    Cypher port already occupied by an unknown process;
    runner-owned temp root already exists;
    sidecar device label directory already exists;
    sidecar conversation directory already exists;
    Comms state file already exists outside runner-owned temp root;
    Cypher DB path exists outside runner-owned temp root;
    required repo paths are missing;
    required toolchains are missing.

Allowed cleanup:

    runner-owned temp root created by this profile invocation;
    profile-owned temporary Cypher DB;
    profile-owned logs/evidence files.

Disallowed cleanup:

    user trust.json;
    user trust-events.jsonl;
    user identity-candidates.json;
    unknown .carbonstack-openmls-sidecar-state roots;
    non-profile sidecar device labels;
    non-profile provider storage;
    non-profile Cypher DBs;
    repo source/docs;
    release artifacts not created by the profile.

Cleanup must not become recovery, reset, re-enrollment, or key replacement.

### 0.8 Required Future Profile Sequence and Assertions

Future profile should perform:

    repo/path/toolchain checks;
    package tests or targeted tests;
    fresh temp root creation;
    local Cypher start with temp DB;
    Cypher health check;
    Alice/Bob Comms init;
    Alice/Bob dev invite creation and claim;
    Alice/Bob device registration;
    Relay Space creation;
    Alice/Bob Relay Space routing member registration;
    fresh sidecar identity creation;
    Alice sidecar conversation creation and load check;
    no-ack smoke run;
    ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1 smoke run using separate fresh generated state or separate fresh Relay Space/Cypher DB;
    DB summary capture;
    trust/candidate before/after capture;
    registry/public-surface assertion;
    final status output.

No-ack subrun should assert:

    KeyPackage envelope exists and is queued;
    Welcome envelope exists and is queued;
    no envelope_acks rows exist;
    join output includes status joined;
    join output includes ack_requested false;
    join output includes welcome_acked false;
    checked trust/candidate files are absent or unchanged.

ACK_AFTER_JOIN subrun should assert:

    KeyPackage envelope exists and is queued;
    Welcome envelope exists and is acknowledged;
    exactly one envelope_acks row exists;
    ack row references the Welcome envelope;
    join output includes status joined;
    join output includes ack_requested true;
    join output includes welcome_acked true;
    join output includes ack_delivery_state acknowledged;
    checked trust/candidate files are absent or unchanged.

Do not reuse the no-ack run's queued Welcome for the ack run.

### 0.9 Trust/Candidate and Registry/Public-Surface Boundaries

Future profile must not mutate:

    trust.json;
    trust-events.jsonl;
    identity-candidates.json;
    verified device state;
    candidate acceptance state;
    key replacement state;
    recovery state.

Initial validation may check only runner-owned expected paths and current Comms state-dir paths.

It must not overclaim broad trust/candidate safety from absence checks.

If the future runner profile becomes callable and is added to the registry, registry metadata must be:

    audience: developer;
    maturity: experimental;
    include_in_front_readme: false;
    explicit nonclaims preserved.

Do not promote it in the front README during first implementation.

    sidecar join failure;

### 0.5 v0.5.50 Deep Recon / Decision Context

v0.5.50 started with a validation-profile / ACK_AFTER_JOIN deep recon.

Important recon results:

    repo heads and status were clean at the v0.5.49 baseline;
    v0.5.49 docs confirmed ACK_AFTER_JOIN evidence remained explicitly missing;
    Comms command surface confirmed openmls-relay-join-dev supports --ack-after-join;
    script surface confirmed ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1 maps to --ack-after-join;
    Comms unit tests already cover no-ack behavior, ack-after-join behavior, sidecar join failure/no-ack behavior, and ack error handling seams;
    Cypher scoped ack routes and DB ack behavior exist;
    compact recon validation passed across Comms, Cypher, runner tests, and runner doctor.

One recon blunder:

    the initial sqlite3 inline DB inspection used .headers/.mode dot commands inside a quoted SQL string, which made SQLite treat them as SQL and error.
    This was a recon-command issue only, not a code failure.
    The later v0.5.50 ACK smoke used proper sqlite3 heredoc syntax and produced DB counts/envelope/ack evidence.

Decision after recon:

    run a fresh ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1 smoke proof with fresh v0.5.50 Cypher DB, Comms states, Relay Space, routing members, sidecar labels, and conversation.
    Do not reuse the v0.5.49 no-ack Relay Space/state because the Welcome was intentionally left unacked.

The live ACK_AFTER_JOIN smoke script completed all three expected steps.

#### Step 1: Bob submits KeyPackage to Alice through Relay Space

Observed evidence:

    command: openmls-relay-keypackage-submit-dev

### 0.10 Ack Boundary Now Has Both Sides Evidenced

Combined v0.5.49 and v0.5.50 evidence supports:

    v0.5.49 no-ack run:
        Welcome join succeeded;
        ack_requested: false;
        welcome_acked: false.

    v0.5.50 ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1 run:
        Welcome join succeeded;
        ack_requested: true;
        welcome_acked: true;
        Welcome envelope delivery_state became acknowledged;
        exactly one envelope_acks row existed for the Welcome envelope.

Current rule remains:

    KeyPackage is not acked by the smoke script.
    Welcome is not acked by default.
    Welcome may be acked only by explicit ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1 / --ack-after-join.
    Existing command implementation gates that ack after sidecar conversation-join success.

Ack remains:

    delivery/local-processing state;
    not identity proof;
    not local verification;
    not provider trust;
    not a local-backbone claim.

v0.5.50 provides ACK_AFTER_JOIN evidence and DB ack evidence, but still does not add a validation profile.

Before a validation profile, the project still needs:

    dedicated validation-profile design;
    generated-state ownership rules;
    generated-state cleanup rules;
    safe refusal if expected generated state already exists;
    fresh sidecar label/state strategy or isolated sidecar state roots;
    exact Cypher DB/server lifecycle ownership;
    exact Comms state file lifecycle ownership;
    stronger trust/candidate nonmutation checks;
    failure-path evidence or tests tied to the smoke harness;
    registry/front README/public-surface claim checks;
    exact profile claim/nonclaim language.

The next rung should be validation-profile design, not direct implementation unless recon makes the generated-state/cleanup design obviously safe.

### 0.6 Live Setup and Discovery Lessons

Several live setup attempts produced important continuity lessons before the successful smoke proof.

#### Placeholder env failure

A first attempt exported literal placeholder values:

    /path/to/alice-state.json
    /path/to/bob-state.json
    your-relay-space-id
    alice-cypher-device-id
    bob-cypher-device-id
    alice-sidecar-label
    bob-sidecar-label
    alice-conversation-label
    bob-conversation-label

The script accepted them as “set,” then failed immediately because `/path/to/bob-state.json` did not exist.

Lesson:

    required-env checks only prove variables are nonempty;
    v0.5.50+ validation work needs existence/shape checks for state files and likely health checks for Cypher before running the sequence.

#### Cypher not running

A setup attempt initialized Alice/Bob Comms state files but failed to create/claim invites because Cypher was not reachable:

    dial tcp 127.0.0.1:8080: connect: connection refused

That left state files with empty:

    account_id;
    device_id;
    display_name;
    device_label.

Lesson:

    smoke setup must start/health-check Cypher before invite/account/device setup;
    failed Comms state files should not be reused.

#### Cypher/Relay Space discovery

Discovery confirmed:

    Cypher default address: CYPHER_ADDR=:8080;
    Cypher default DB path: CYPHER_DB=cypher.db;
    Cypher migrations env: CYPHER_MIGRATIONS;
    Cypher dev invite env: CYPHER_DEV_INVITE=dev-invite;
    health route: GET /v0/health;
    dev invite routes exist;
    device registration route exists;
    Relay Space create/list/get routes exist;
    Relay Space member register/list routes exist;
    Relay Space-scoped envelope submit/inbox/ack routes exist.

#### Fresh local Cypher setup succeeded

Successful setup used:

    CYPHER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080
    CYPHER_DB=/tmp/carbonstack-v0549-cypher.db
    CYPHER_ADDR=:8080
    CYPHER_MIGRATIONS=$HOME/repos/carbonstack_umbrella/carbonstack-cypher/migrations
    CYPHER_DEV_INVITE=dev-invite

Cypher started and health returned:

    {"api_version":"v0","service":"carbonstack-cypher","status":"ok"}

Fresh Comms state files were created under `/tmp`.

Fresh Alice/Bob accounts and devices were created.

Fresh Relay Space was created:

    RELAY_SPACE_ID=v0549-smoke-relay-space

Both devices were registered as active routing members.

#### Sidecar state reuse failure

First no-ack smoke attempt against older sidecar labels failed before KeyPackage submission:

    device provider storage already exists:
    .carbonstack-openmls-sidecar-state/dev/devices/carbonstack-bob-device/provider-storage.json

This was not a Relay Space/Cypher failure.

Lesson:

    smoke runs need fresh sidecar labels/state or explicit cleanup ownership;
    v0.5.50+ generated-state planning must include sidecar identity/conversation state lifecycle;
    do not blindly reuse old OpenMLS sidecar labels/conversations in smoke proof.

#### Fresh sidecar setup succeeded

Successful fresh sidecar setup used:

    ALICE_SIDECAR_LABEL=carbonstack-v0549-alice-device
    BOB_SIDECAR_LABEL=carbonstack-v0549-bob-device
    ALICE_CONVERSATION_LABEL=carbonstack-v0549-conversation
    BOB_CONVERSATION_LABEL=carbonstack-v0549-conversation

Fresh sidecar identities were created.

Alice conversation was created and load-checked successfully.

### 0.7 Live No-Ack Smoke Proof Success

The successful no-ack live smoke proof used:

    ALICE_STATE=/tmp/carbonstack-v0549-alice-state.json
    BOB_STATE=/tmp/carbonstack-v0549-bob-state.json
    RELAY_SPACE_ID=v0549-smoke-relay-space
    ALICE_DEVICE_ID=77d27b1a-92bf-4727-ad37-6a94ef153e5e
    BOB_DEVICE_ID=d1c8c0a5-30b4-41d0-996c-e8eb760c88ee
    ALICE_SIDECAR_LABEL=carbonstack-v0549-alice-device
    BOB_SIDECAR_LABEL=carbonstack-v0549-bob-device
    ALICE_CONVERSATION_LABEL=carbonstack-v0549-conversation
    BOB_CONVERSATION_LABEL=carbonstack-v0549-conversation
    ACK_AFTER_JOIN unset

The script completed all three expected steps.

#### Step 1: Bob submits KeyPackage to Alice through Relay Space

Observed evidence:

    openmls relay keypackage submit dev
    command: openmls-relay-keypackage-submit-dev
    status: sent
    relay_space_id: v0549-smoke-relay-space
    sidecar_command: public-bundle-export
    sidecar_device_label: carbonstack-v0549-bob-device
    content_type: carbonstack.mls.keypackage.v0
    protocol_version: carbonstack-openmls-sidecar-v0
    delivery_state: queued
    payload_size_bytes: 302

This proves only that Bob exported a dev OpenMLS KeyPackage artifact and submitted it through the Relay Space envelope path to Alice.

#### Step 2: Alice consumes KeyPackage, runs add-member, submits Welcome to Bob

Observed evidence:

    openmls relay add-member dev
    command: openmls-relay-add-member-dev
    status: welcome_created_and_sent
    sidecar_command: conversation-add-member
    sidecar_device_label: carbonstack-v0549-alice-device
    sidecar_conversation_label: carbonstack-v0549-conversation
    welcome_recipient_device_id: d1c8c0a5-30b4-41d0-996c-e8eb760c88ee
    welcome_delivery_state: queued
    welcome_payload_size_bytes: 893
    keypackage_acked: false
    welcome_acked: false
    member_added: true
    welcome_artifact_written: true
    group_reloadable: true
    member_count_before: 1
    member_count_after: 2
    epoch_before: GroupEpoch(0)
    epoch_after: GroupEpoch(1)

This proves only that Alice consumed the queued KeyPackage artifact, ran dev sidecar conversation-add-member, produced a Welcome artifact, and submitted it through the Relay Space envelope path to Bob.

#### Step 3: Bob consumes Welcome and runs conversation-join

Observed evidence:

    openmls relay join dev
    command: openmls-relay-join-dev
    status: joined
    sidecar_command: conversation-join
    sidecar_device_label: carbonstack-v0549-bob-device
    sidecar_conversation_label: carbonstack-v0549-conversation
    ack_requested: false
    welcome_acked: false
    joined: true
    group_reloadable: true
    member_count: 2
    epoch: GroupEpoch(1)

This proves only that Bob consumed the queued Welcome artifact and the dev sidecar conversation-join path reported a joined/reloadable group.

Because ACK_AFTER_JOIN was unset, scoped Welcome ack was not requested.

### 0.10 Ack Boundary Preserved

The successful live smoke proof was no-ack.

Observed:

    ACK_AFTER_JOIN not set to 1;
    command: openmls-relay-join-dev;
    ack_requested: false;
    welcome_acked: false.

Current rule remains:

    KeyPackage is not acked by the smoke script.
    Welcome is not acked by default.
    Welcome may be acked only by explicit ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1 / --ack-after-join.
    Existing v0.5.46 command implementation gates that ack after sidecar conversation-join success.

v0.5.49 did not run the ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1 path.

Do not infer scoped ack evidence from this no-ack run.

v0.5.48 implements the next safe smoke-proof support layer:

    add a main CarbonStack narrow smoke-proof runbook;
    add a Comms component smoke-proof runbook;
    add a thin Comms dev helper script under scripts/ that sequences existing dev commands;
    add minimal hidden registry coverage for that script because the runner treats callable scripts as command-surface artifacts.

The v0.5.48 helper script sequences:

    Bob submits KeyPackage to Alice through Relay Space;
    Alice consumes KeyPackage, runs add-member, and submits Welcome to Bob;
    Bob consumes Welcome and runs conversation-join;
    optionally, Bob requests scoped Welcome ack only after join success through ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1.

This remains a dev/pre-alpha command-sequencing proof, not a validation profile and not local-backbone.

### 0.5 Smoke-Proof Script Shape

Script path:

    carbonstack-comms/scripts/openmls-relay-narrow-join-smoke-dev.sh

Required environment:

    ALICE_STATE
    BOB_STATE
    RELAY_SPACE_ID
    ALICE_DEVICE_ID
    BOB_DEVICE_ID
    ALICE_SIDECAR_LABEL
    BOB_SIDECAR_LABEL
    ALICE_CONVERSATION_LABEL
    BOB_CONVERSATION_LABEL

Optional environment:

    COMMS_DIR
    ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1

Script sequence:

    1. Bob submits a KeyPackage to Alice:
        go run ./cmd/comms openmls-relay-keypackage-submit-dev

    2. Alice consumes the KeyPackage, runs add-member, and submits Welcome to Bob:
        go run ./cmd/comms openmls-relay-add-member-dev

    3. Bob consumes the Welcome and runs conversation-join:
        go run ./cmd/comms openmls-relay-join-dev

If ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1:

    step 3 adds --ack-after-join.

Otherwise:

    step 3 does not request scoped Welcome ack.

The script does not create accounts, devices, Relay Spaces, or conversations.

The script does not start Cypher.

The script does not mutate trust/candidate state directly.

### 0.6 Smoke-Proof Evidence Target

The main runbook defines expected evidence:

KeyPackage submit output should include:

    command: openmls-relay-keypackage-submit-dev
    status: sent
    content_type: application/vnd.carbonstack.openmls.keypackage
    envelope_id:

Add-member output should include:

    command: openmls-relay-add-member-dev
    status: welcome_created_and_sent
    sidecar_command: conversation-add-member
    welcome_envelope_id:
    keypackage_acked: false
    welcome_acked: false

Join output without ack should include:

    command: openmls-relay-join-dev
    status: joined
    sidecar_command: conversation-join
    ack_requested: false
    welcome_acked: false

Join output with ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1 should include:

    command: openmls-relay-join-dev
    status: joined
    ack_requested: true
    welcome_acked: true
    ack_envelope_id:
    ack_delivery_state:

### 0.7 Ack Boundary Preserved

v0.5.48 does not change ack semantics.

Current smoke-proof rule:

    KeyPackage is not acked by the smoke script.
    Welcome is not acked by default.
    Welcome may be acked only by explicit ACK_AFTER_JOIN=1 / --ack-after-join.
    Existing v0.5.46 command implementation gates that ack after sidecar conversation-join success.

Ack remains:

    not identity proof;
    not local verification;
    not provider trust;
    not a local-backbone claim.

### 0.8 Trust / Candidate Boundary Preserved

v0.5.48 does not mutate:

    trust.json;
    trust-events.jsonl;
    identity-candidates.json;
    verified device state;
    candidate acceptance state;
    key replacement state;
    recovery state.

The smoke proof must not treat:

    Relay Space membership;
    KeyPackage presence;
    Welcome presence;
    sidecar add-member success;
    sidecar conversation-join success;
    group reloadability;
    member count;
    epoch movement;
    scoped ack;

as local verification.

Provider/OpenMLS identity-relevant material remains unverified until a future candidate/review/verification path handles it.

Candidate observation remains deferred and must not be hidden inside the smoke proof.

### 0.5 Current Dev Scaffold State

The current Relay Space OpenMLS dev scaffold includes:

    openmls-relay-keypackage-submit-dev;

    openmls-relay-welcome-submit-dev;

The current dev path can express:

This remains explicit dev/pre-alpha scaffolding, not production UX.

### 0.6 Ack Boundary Stabilized

v0.5.47 documents the ack invariants instead of expanding implementation.

Current invariants:

    KeyPackage envelopes are not acked merely because they were downloaded or written.
    KeyPackage ack must wait for successful add-member or an explicitly defined safe terminal handling path.
    Welcome envelopes are not acked merely because they were downloaded or written.
    Welcome ack must wait for successful conversation-join.
    Application-message envelopes must wait for successful message-open.

Current v0.5.46 implementation state:

    openmls-relay-join-dev does not ack by default.
    openmls-relay-join-dev only attempts scoped ack when --ack-after-join is explicitly passed.
    scoped ack happens after sidecar conversation-join returns success.
    tests prove no ack on Welcome write failure.
    tests prove no ack on sidecar join failure.

### 0.7 Narrow Smoke-Proof Goal

The next narrow smoke proof should prove one local/dev path only:

    Alice and Bob have ready Comms/Cypher state.
    Bob exports a KeyPackage and submits it to a Relay Space for Alice.
    Alice retrieves Bob's KeyPackage from the Relay Space and writes it locally.
    Alice runs sidecar conversation-add-member with that KeyPackage.
    Alice submits the produced Welcome back through the same Relay Space for Bob.
    Bob retrieves the Welcome and writes it locally.
    Bob runs sidecar conversation-join.
    Optional: Bob scoped-acks the Welcome only after successful join using --ack-after-join.

Allowed demonstration claim:

    The dev scaffold can complete the KeyPackage -> Welcome -> join leg in a bounded local/dev path.

Forbidden claims:

    general local-backbone;
    production messaging path;
    hostile-server-safe path;
    verified identity;
    secure enrollment;
    metadata-private routing.

    it records ack-after-join as opt-in and gated, not a general trust signal;
    it preserves the path toward a narrow v0.5.48 smoke proof.

### 0.5 Dev Command Added

`openmls-relay-join-dev`:

    retrieves Relay Space-scoped Welcome envelopes for the local Cypher device;
    writes the first Welcome artifact to a temp file;
    runs the sidecar `conversation-join` command using that written Welcome;
    prints joined, group_reloadable, member_count, epoch, join_summary_path_hint, conversation_state_path_hint, conversation_summary_path_hint, and provider_storage_path_hint when present;
    defaults ack_requested:false and welcome_acked:false;
    supports explicit --ack-after-join;
    if --ack-after-join is passed, a scoped Welcome ack is sent only after sidecar conversation-join returns success;
    warns that it is dev/pre-alpha and not identity verification, local-backbone, or production UX.

### 0.6 Ack Boundary Updated but Preserved

v0.5.46 is the first rung that introduces scoped ack in a Relay Space OpenMLS dev command, but only in an explicit, gated form.

Default behavior:

    no scoped ack;
    ack_requested:false;
    welcome_acked:false.

Optional behavior:

    --ack-after-join enables scoped Welcome ack;
    ack is called only after sidecar conversation-join returns success;
    ack uses relay_space_id, Welcome envelope_id, and local recipient device_id.

Tests prove:

    default join path does not ack;
    --ack-after-join acks only on successful sidecar join;
    sidecar join failure does not ack;
    Welcome write failure does not ack;
    no Welcome envelope state fails before ack.

Current rule remains:

    KeyPackage envelopes:
        ack only after successful add-member or explicit safe terminal handling.
    Welcome envelopes:
        ack only after successful conversation-join.
    Application-message envelopes:
        ack only after successful message-open.

v0.5.46 only implements the Welcome side of that rule in a dev/pre-alpha command and keeps it opt-in.

### 0.7 Trust / Candidate Boundary Preserved

v0.5.46 does not mutate:

    trust.json;
    identity-candidates.json;
    verified device state;
    candidate acceptance state;
    key replacement state;
    recovery state.

The new command does not claim that:

    a Relay Space Welcome envelope verifies identity;
    a written Welcome verifies identity;
    sidecar conversation-join verifies identity;
    provider membership equals local verification;
    joined:true verifies identity;
    group_reloadable:true verifies identity;
    member_count or epoch is local trust;
    scoped ack is local verification.

Provider/OpenMLS membership remains separate from local verification.

### 0.8 Scope Preserved

v0.5.46 does not:

    create a one-command full join from both parties;
    combine KeyPackage export, add-member, Welcome send, Welcome join, and ack into one broad command;
    mutate trust.json;
    mutate identity-candidates.json;
    accept provider-observed identities;
    replace keys;
    implement candidate observation;
    implement validation profile;
    implement full local-backbone;
    promote commands in front README;
    claim metadata privacy;
    claim hostile-server safety;
    claim production readiness;
    implement vault/PQ/hybrid.

The v0.5.42 roadmap projected:

    v0.5.43 KeyPackage/Welcome transport preflight;
    v0.5.44 KeyPackage Relay Space transport slice;
    v0.5.45 Welcome Relay Space transport slice;
    v0.5.46 join-command scaffolding boundary;

Reality has safely compressed the early transport/scaffold work:

    v0.5.45 added inviter-side KeyPackage -> add-member -> Welcome submit scaffold;
    v0.5.46 added invitee-side Welcome -> conversation-join scaffold and opt-in ack-after-join.

This means the project now has practical dev command coverage for the intended KeyPackage -> add-member -> Welcome -> join sequence, though it is still not a full local-backbone claim.

The remaining risky pieces:

    full local-backbone proof;

v0.5.46 is the first dev/pre-alpha Relay Space invitee-side join scaffold.

Its significance is narrow but important:

    the inviter-side v0.5.45 add-member/Welcome-send leg now has an invitee-side counterpart;
    the invitee can retrieve a Relay Space Welcome and feed it to sidecar conversation-join through a dev command;
    scoped Welcome ack is now possible but explicit and gated after sidecar join success;
    tests prove no ack occurs on sidecar join failure or Welcome write failure;
    KeyPackage -> add-member -> Welcome -> join is now represented as explicit dev scaffolding;
    local verification remains separate;
    validation profile remains deferred.
