    submits the produced Welcome artifact back through Relay Space;
    defaults Welcome recipient to the KeyPackage sender device;
    allows explicit Welcome recipient override with --welcome-to-device;
    prints member_added, welcome_artifact_written, group_reloadable, member_count_before, member_count_after, epoch_before, and epoch_after when present;
    prints keypackage_acked:false and welcome_acked:false;
    warns that it is dev/pre-alpha and not join automation, identity verification, local-backbone, or production UX.

### 0.6 Ack Boundary Preserved

v0.5.45 deliberately does not ack.

Current command behavior:

    KeyPackage retrieval/write:
        no ack.
    Sidecar add-member:
        no KeyPackage ack.
    Welcome submit:
        no Welcome ack.
    Conversation join:
        not run.

Current rule remains:

    KeyPackage envelopes:
        ack only after successful add-member or explicit safe terminal handling.
    Welcome envelopes:
        ack only after successful conversation-join.
    Application-message envelopes:
        ack only after successful message-open.

v0.5.45 still avoids scoped ack because it stops before invitee-side conversation-join and because KeyPackage terminal-handling policy needs a dedicated review/test rung.

### 0.7 Trust / Candidate Boundary Preserved

v0.5.45 does not mutate:

    trust.json;
    identity-candidates.json;
    verified device state;
    candidate acceptance state;
    key replacement state;
    recovery state.

The new command does not claim that:

    a Relay Space KeyPackage envelope verifies identity;
    a written KeyPackage verifies identity;
    sidecar conversation-add-member verifies identity;
    a Welcome artifact verifies identity;
    Welcome submission proves the invitee joined;
    provider membership equals local verification;
    member_count_after or epoch_after is local trust.

Provider/OpenMLS membership remains separate from local verification.

### 0.8 Scope Preserved

v0.5.45 does not:

    run sidecar conversation-join;
    read/write Welcome inbox as part of this command;
    add scoped ack helper;
    ack after add-member;
    ack after Welcome submit;
    create a one-command full join;
    mutate trust.json;
    mutate identity-candidates.json;
    accept provider-observed identities;
    replace keys;
    implement candidate observation;
    implement validation profile;
    implement full local-backbone;
    claim metadata privacy;
    claim hostile-server safety;
    claim production readiness;
    implement vault/PQ/hybrid.

The risky pieces remain deferred:

### 0.15 Significance

v0.5.45 is the first dev/pre-alpha Relay Space sidecar-operation scaffold.

Its significance is narrow but important:

    the invitee's Relay Space KeyPackage can now be consumed by an inviter-side add-member command;
    the inviter-side sidecar can produce a Welcome from that KeyPackage;
    that Welcome can be submitted back through Relay Space in the same bounded dev command;
    KeyPackage -> add-member -> Welcome transport now has a practical dev scaffold;
    invitee-side join remains a separate future rung;
    scoped ack remains deliberately absent;
    local verification remains separate.

          keeps sender_device_id, recipient_device_id, relay_space_id, artifact_path, and client_created_at explicit.

      RelaySpaceOpenMLSArtifactInbox:
          requires non-empty relay_space_id;
          requires non-empty device_id;

          calls c.RelaySpaceInbox;

### 0.5 Helper Methods Implemented

`SubmitRelaySpaceKeyPackageEnvelope`:

    accepts client.CypherClient;
    accepts relay_space_id;
    accepts sender_device_id;
    accepts recipient_device_id;
    accepts artifact path;
    accepts optional client_created_at;
    calls SubmitRelaySpaceOpenMLSArtifactEnvelope with ArtifactKindKeyPackage;
    returns client.SubmitRelaySpaceEnvelopeResponse.

`SubmitRelaySpaceWelcomeEnvelope`:

    accepts client.CypherClient;
    accepts relay_space_id;
    accepts sender_device_id;
    accepts recipient_device_id;
    accepts artifact path;
    accepts optional client_created_at;
    calls SubmitRelaySpaceOpenMLSArtifactEnvelope with ArtifactKindWelcome;
    returns client.SubmitRelaySpaceEnvelopeResponse.

`RelaySpaceOpenMLSArtifactInbox`:

    accepts client.CypherClient;
    accepts relay_space_id;
    accepts device_id;
    accepts artifact kind;
    rejects missing relay_space_id;
    rejects missing device_id;
    rejects unsupported artifact kind;
    calls c.RelaySpaceInbox;
    filters envelopes to those whose content_type matches the requested OpenMLS artifact kind;
    returns []client.RelaySpaceEnvelopeRecord.

`WriteRelaySpaceKeyPackageFromEnvelope`:

    accepts output path;
    accepts client.RelaySpaceEnvelopeRecord;
    rejects envelopes whose content_type is not ContentTypeOpenMLSKeyPackage;
    delegates to WriteOpenMLSArtifactFromRelaySpaceEnvelope.

`WriteRelaySpaceWelcomeFromEnvelope`:

    accepts output path;
    accepts client.RelaySpaceEnvelopeRecord;
    rejects envelopes whose content_type is not ContentTypeOpenMLSWelcome;
    delegates to WriteOpenMLSArtifactFromRelaySpaceEnvelope.

### 0.6 Boundary Preserved

v0.5.43 preserves the v0.5.42 provider/OpenMLS join boundary.

The new helpers move and filter artifacts only.

They do not:

    export a KeyPackage from sidecar;
    run conversation-add-member;
    create a Welcome artifact by themselves;
    run conversation-join;
    message-open application messages;
    ack any envelope;
    mutate trust.json;
    mutate identity-candidates.json;
    mark a device verified;
    accept a candidate identity;
    replace known key material;
    decide provider membership safety;
    decide local verification;
    claim metadata privacy;
    claim hostile-server safety.

This matters because KeyPackage and Welcome artifact presence is not a proof of local trust or successful join.

### 0.7 Ack Boundary Preserved

v0.5.43 deliberately does not add a scoped ack helper.

Reason:

    v0.5.40 already exposed client.AckRelaySpaceEnvelope;
    v0.5.41 deliberately avoided bridge-level scoped ack;
    v0.5.42 documented that Welcome ack must happen only after successful conversation-join;
    v0.5.43 only retrieves/writes artifacts and does not run sidecar conversation-join;
    adding an ack helper here would make ack-before-sidecar-success easier.

Current rule remains:

    KeyPackage envelopes:
        ack only after successful add-member or explicit safe terminal handling.
    Welcome envelopes:
        ack only after successful conversation-join.
    Application-message envelopes:
        ack only after successful message-open.

Download, filter, or write success is not ack eligibility.

### 0.8 Roadmap Alignment Note

The v0.5.42 roadmap refresh originally split near-term work into:

    v0.5.43 KeyPackage/Welcome transport preflight;
    v0.5.44 KeyPackage Relay Space transport slice;
    v0.5.45 Welcome Relay Space transport slice;
    v0.5.46 join-command scaffolding boundary;
    v0.5.47 candidate observation boundary;
    v0.5.48 narrow join smoke proof.

v0.5.43 collapsed the safe helper-level parts of v0.5.44 and v0.5.45 into one implementation rung after recon confirmed the helper substrate was narrow enough.

This does not mean v0.5.44/v0.5.45 are obsolete as broader runtime/dev-command goals. It means helper-level transport substrate is now available earlier than the roadmap's hypothetical split.

The next rung should reassess the plan before moving to any dev-command scaffolding or sidecar orchestration.

### 0.9 Scope Preserved

v0.5.43 does not:

    wire helpers into Comms app/runtime commands;
    add dev command scaffolding;
    run sidecar public-bundle-export;
    run sidecar conversation-add-member;
    run sidecar conversation-join;
    add bridge-level scoped ack helper;
    add provider live-flow;
    automate OpenMLS join;
    mutate trust.json;
    mutate identity-candidates.json;
    add candidate observation from KeyPackage/Welcome material;
    mark any provider-observed identity verified;
    add local-backbone validation profile;
    add CLI/registry entries;
    implement full local-backbone;
    implement hostile-server harnesses;
    implement deployability/operator work;
    implement vault/PQ/hybrid;
    make production/security/audit claims.

### 0.10 Why Helper-Level Collapse Was Acceptable

The helper-level collapse was acceptable because:

    v0.5.43 did not wire runtime or sidecar commands;
    KeyPackage and Welcome submit helpers share the same existing scoped artifact submit path;
    KeyPackage and Welcome writer helpers share the same existing Relay Space artifact writer path;
    the new inbox helper only filters by known content type;
    tests use fake HTTP server behavior and do not run a real sidecar join;
    no ack helper was added;
    no trust/candidate mutation was added;
    no CLI/registry surface was exposed.

This captures the useful transport substrate without crossing into full join automation.

### 0.3 Changed Surfaces

`carbonstack`:

    docs/190-v0.5.42-provider-openmls-join-wiring-plan-v0.md
      Added the main planning-only decision document.
      Defines purpose, current substrate, current OpenMLS sidecar/app surfaces, and the core distinction between Relay Space routing, OpenMLS provider/group membership, and local verification.
      Defines preferred artifact order:
          Relay Space exists;
          routing members exist;
          invitee exports KeyPackage/public bundle;
          invitee submits KeyPackage artifact through Relay Space-scoped envelope;
          inviter retrieves KeyPackage;
          inviter runs conversation-add-member;
          sidecar creates Welcome artifact;
          inviter submits Welcome through Relay Space-scoped envelope;
          invitee retrieves Welcome;
          invitee runs conversation-join;
          invitee acks Welcome only after join succeeds;
          application messages remain later.
      Defines candidate observation rule:
          provider/OpenMLS identity-relevant material may become candidate/unverified material;
          it must not directly become verified trust, key replacement, or local verified state.
      Defines provider membership vs local verification:
          successful provider/group membership does not equal verified identity.
      Defines ack timing:
          KeyPackage ack only after successful add-member or explicit safe terminal handling;
          Welcome ack only after successful conversation-join;
          application-message ack only after message-open succeeds.
      Defines forbidden automatic mutations:
          no automatic verified status;
          no trust.json mutation from Relay Space or provider membership alone;
          no identity-candidate acceptance by default;
          no silent key replacement;
          no recovery bypass.
      Defines future ladder:
          after v0.5.42, refresh roadmap;
          v0.5.43 first narrow KeyPackage/Welcome Relay Space artifact transport implementation if recon confirms a safe slice;
          later candidate observation, dev join flow, validation profile, and CLI/registry only after boundaries are proven.

`carbonstack-comms`:

    docs/23-provider-openmls-join-wiring-plan-v0.md
      Added Comms component boundary/planning doc.
      Records current Comms state:
          unscoped Cypher client methods;
          Relay Space Cypher client methods;

          Relay Space-aware OpenMLS artifact bridge helpers;
          OpenMLS sidecar dev commands for identity, KeyPackage export, conversation create, add-member, join, message protect, and message open;
          existing unscoped openmls-send-dev and openmls-inbox-dev;
          ack-after-message-open behavior in the existing inbox path.
      Defines future Comms join path:
          invitee exports KeyPackage;
          invitee submits KeyPackage through Relay Space-scoped envelope;
          inviter receives KeyPackage;
          inviter runs conversation-add-member;
          inviter submits Welcome through Relay Space-scoped envelope;
          invitee receives Welcome;
          invitee runs conversation-join;
          invitee acks Welcome only after join succeeds.
      Reasserts candidate/trust rule:
          observed identity material may enter candidate observation/review paths only;
          no direct trust.json mutation, key replacement, verification, or recovery bypass.

### 0.5 Planning Decisions Captured

v0.5.42 captured these core decisions:

    provider/OpenMLS join wiring must be staged, not implemented as one broad live-flow;
    Relay Space is routing/conversation infrastructure only;
    OpenMLS provider/group membership is cryptographic group membership only;
    local verification is a separate trust ceremony/state transition;
    KeyPackage and Welcome artifact movement must be explicit and Relay Space-scoped;
    provider/OpenMLS identity-relevant material is candidate/unverified material until local verification says otherwise;
    successful sidecar add-member, Welcome creation, join, epoch advancement, or group reloadability does not equal verified identity;
    ack must remain tied to successful local sidecar processing;
    future implementation must avoid automatic trust mutation, key replacement, candidate acceptance, or recovery bypass;
    first future implementation should be a narrow KeyPackage/Welcome artifact transport slice only if recon confirms a safe path.

### 0.6 Ack Boundary Preserved

v0.5.42 preserves and strengthens the ack boundary.

Current principle:

    Ack is not a download receipt.
    Ack is not a Relay Space membership proof.
    Ack is not provider membership proof.
    Ack is not artifact write proof by itself.
    Ack is evidence that local sidecar processing succeeded or that a future explicit safe-terminal handling design has been documented.

Planned future rules:

    KeyPackage envelopes:
        ack only after successful add-member or explicit safe terminal handling.
    Welcome envelopes:
        ack only after successful conversation-join.
    Application-message envelopes:
        ack only after successful message-open.

This is especially important because v0.5.40 exposed client.AckRelaySpaceEnvelope and v0.5.41 deliberately avoided a bridge-level scoped ack helper.

### 0.7 Candidate / Trust Boundary Preserved

v0.5.42 preserves the trust boundary.

Provider/OpenMLS join wiring may observe identity-relevant material, but that material remains:

    candidate;
    unverified;
    local-review-bound;
    not accepted automatically.

Do not convert any of the following into verified local trust:

    Relay Space membership;
    Relay Space invite possession;
    QR scan;
    scoped envelope presence;
    KeyPackage artifact presence;
    Welcome artifact presence;
    successful add-member;
    successful conversation-join;
    provider member count;
    epoch advancement;
    group reloadability;
    bridge helper success;
    sidecar command success by itself.

Local verification remains separate.

### 0.8 Scope Preserved

v0.5.42 does not:

    implement provider live-flow;
    implement OpenMLS join automation;
    add KeyPackage/Welcome transport code;
    wire Relay Space helpers into Comms app/runtime commands;
    change Comms OpenMLS send/inbox command behavior;
    change Cypher routes;
    change Cypher DB schema;
    mutate trust.json;
    mutate identity-candidates.json;
    add candidate observation from provider/OpenMLS material;
    add bridge-level scoped ack helper;
    add local-backbone validation profile;
    add CLI/registry entries;
    implement full local-backbone;
    implement destructive reset/recovery/re-enrollment;
    implement vault/PQ/hybrid;
    make metadata privacy claims;
    make hostile-server safety claims;
    make production/security/audit claims.

### 0.9 Why Planning-Only Was Correct

v0.5.42 stayed planning-only because provider/OpenMLS join wiring touches a high-risk convergence point:

    Relay Space routing;
    KeyPackage and Welcome artifact movement;
    OpenMLS group membership;
    provider-observed identity material;
    candidate observation;
    local trust state;
    ack-after-sidecar-success policy;
    future validation profile claims.

Implementing code before documenting these boundaries would risk collapsing routing success into trust success.

The planning docs now define the boundaries that future implementation must obey.

### 0.5 Helper Methods Implemented

`SubmitRelaySpaceOpenMLSArtifactEnvelope`:

    accepts client.CypherClient;
    accepts relay_space_id;
    accepts sender_device_id;
    accepts recipient_device_id;
    accepts artifact kind;
    accepts artifact path;
    accepts optional client_created_at;
    rejects missing relay_space_id;
    rejects unsupported artifact kind;
    reads artifact payload and base64-encodes it;
    uses ProtocolVersionOpenMLSSidecar;
    calls c.SubmitRelaySpaceEnvelope;
    returns client.SubmitRelaySpaceEnvelopeResponse.

`WriteOpenMLSArtifactFromRelaySpaceEnvelope`:

    accepts output path;
    accepts client.RelaySpaceEnvelopeRecord;
    rejects missing relay_space_id;
    converts scoped envelope record to the existing unscoped EnvelopeRecord shape;
    calls WriteOpenMLSArtifactFromEnvelope;
    inherits existing OpenMLS artifact content-type validation;
    inherits existing OpenMLS protocol-version validation;
    inherits existing base64, payload size, and payload SHA-256 metadata validation;
    writes the decoded artifact with the same filesystem behavior as the existing writer.

`relaySpaceEnvelopeToEnvelopeRecord`:

    internal adapter from client.RelaySpaceEnvelopeRecord to client.EnvelopeRecord;
    intentionally drops RelaySpaceID because the existing writer validates artifact payload mechanics, not routing membership.

### 0.6 Routing / Ack Boundary Preserved

v0.5.41 deliberately does not add a bridge-level scoped ack helper.

Reason:

    v0.5.40 client.AckRelaySpaceEnvelope already exists;
    a relay bridge helper named around OpenMLS artifacts could make ack too easy to call before sidecar consume/open;
    project doctrine requires ack only after successful sidecar message-open/consume unless a future negative-ack/quarantine design exists;
    v0.5.41 has no app/runtime sidecar consume proof point;
    therefore bridge-level scoped ack remains deferred until a caller can prove the ack-after-open boundary.

This preserves the earlier ack-after-open rule and avoids turning scoped envelope retrieval into an implicit success condition.

### 0.7 Routing-Only Boundary Preserved

v0.5.41 keeps Relay Space as routing/conversation infrastructure only.

The new helper names and fields use:

    RelaySpace;
    OpenMLSArtifact;
    relay_space_id;
    sender_device_id;
    recipient_device_id;
    content_type;
    protocol_version;
    ciphertext_b64;
    payload_sha256;
    payload_size_bytes;
    delivery_state.

The helper layer does not introduce names or fields implying:

    verified identity;
    trust authority;
    local verification;
    key replacement;
    provider safety truth;
    plaintext authority;
    trust.json mutation;
    identity-candidates.json mutation;
    successful OpenMLS join;
    successful sidecar consume/open.

The helpers submit or write artifacts only. They do not decide trust, provider membership, local verification, or acknowledgement policy.

### 0.8 Scope Preserved

v0.5.41 does not:

    wire Relay Space helpers into Comms app/runtime commands;
    change Comms OpenMLS send/inbox command behavior;
    automate OpenMLS join;
    wire provider live-flow;
    add KeyPackage/Welcome join orchestration;
    mutate trust.json;
    mutate identity-candidates.json;
    add candidate observation from Relay Space membership;
    add bridge-level scoped ack helper;
    add local-backbone validation profile;
    add CLI/registry entries;
    implement full local-backbone;
    implement destructive reset/recovery/re-enrollment;
    implement vault/PQ/hybrid;
    make metadata privacy claims;
    make hostile-server safety claims;
    make production/security/audit claims.

v0.5.41 also does not remove or alter existing unscoped relay bridge helpers. It adds scoped helper variants alongside existing direct device/envelope artifact helpers.

### 0.9 Why Bridge-Helper-Only Was Correct

v0.5.41 chose a bridge-helper-only Comms rung because:

    Cypher has scoped envelope routes;
    Comms has typed Relay Space Cypher client methods;
    existing relay bridge helpers already know how to map OpenMLS artifact kinds to content types and validate payload metadata;
    app/runtime wiring would be premature without a dedicated provider/OpenMLS join plan;
    a helper-only layer gives future runtime code a safer target without embedding raw Relay Space route mechanics;
    tests can prove scoped artifact submit/write behavior without starting real Cypher or sidecar runtime;
    no trust state or candidate identity mutation is needed for a relay bridge helper.

### 0.5 Client Methods Implemented

`CreateRelaySpace`:

    POST /v0/relay-spaces;
    accepts relay_space_id;
    accepts display_label;
    accepts created_by_account_id;
    accepts created_by_device_id;
    returns RelaySpaceResponse.

`ListRelaySpaces`:

    GET /v0/relay-spaces;
    returns ListRelaySpacesResponse.

`GetRelaySpace`:

    GET /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id};
    path-escapes relay_space_id;
    returns RelaySpaceResponse.

`CreateRelaySpaceInvite`:

    POST /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/invites;
    path-escapes relay_space_id;
    accepts CreateRelaySpaceInviteInput;
    returns CreateRelaySpaceInviteResponse with relay_space_invite and invite_token.

`RegisterRelaySpaceMember`:

    POST /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/members;
    path-escapes relay_space_id;
    accepts RegisterRelaySpaceMemberInput;
    returns RelaySpaceMemberResponse.

`ListRelaySpaceMembers`:

    GET /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/members;
    path-escapes relay_space_id;
    returns ListRelaySpaceMembersResponse.

`SubmitRelaySpaceEnvelope`:

    POST /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/envelopes;
    path-escapes relay_space_id;
    accepts sender_device_id;
    accepts recipient_device_id;
    accepts content_type;
    accepts protocol_version;
    accepts ciphertext_b64;
    accepts client_created_at;
    returns SubmitRelaySpaceEnvelopeResponse with envelope_id, relay_space_id, delivery_state, server_received_at, payload_sha256, and payload_size_bytes.

`RelaySpaceInbox`:

    GET /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/devices/{device_id}/envelopes;
    path-escapes relay_space_id and device_id;
    returns RelaySpaceInboxResponse.

`AckRelaySpaceEnvelope`:

    POST /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/envelopes/{envelope_id}/ack;
    path-escapes relay_space_id and envelope_id;
    accepts recipient_device_id;
    returns AckRelaySpaceEnvelopeResponse.

### 0.6 Routing-Only Boundary Preserved

v0.5.40 preserves the routing-only wrapper boundary.

The new Comms client wrapper names and fields use:

    RelaySpace;
    RelaySpaceInvite;
    RelaySpaceMember;
    RoutingMemberID;
    RelaySpaceEnvelope;
    RelaySpaceInbox;
    relay_space_id;
    routing_member_id;
    envelope_id;
    sender_device_id;
    recipient_device_id;
    content_type;
    protocol_version;
    ciphertext_b64;
    payload_sha256;
    payload_size_bytes;
    delivery_state;
    acknowledged_at.

The wrapper does not introduce names or fields implying:

    verified identity;
    trust authority;
    local verification;
    key replacement;
    provider safety truth;
    plaintext authority;
    trust.json mutation;
    identity-candidates.json mutation.

The wrapper calls routes and decodes JSON only. It does not decide trust.

### 0.7 Scope Preserved

v0.5.40 does not:

    wire Relay Space methods into Comms app/runtime commands;
    change Comms OpenMLS runtime behavior;
    automate OpenMLS join;
    wire provider live-flow;
    mutate trust.json;
    mutate identity-candidates.json;
    add candidate observation from Relay Space membership;
    add local-backbone validation profile;
    add CLI/registry entries;
    implement full local-backbone;
    implement destructive reset/recovery/re-enrollment;
    implement vault/PQ/hybrid;
    make metadata privacy claims;
    make hostile-server safety claims;
    make production/security/audit claims.

v0.5.40 also does not remove or alter the existing unscoped Comms Cypher client methods. It adds Relay Space wrapper methods alongside the existing direct device/envelope client methods.

### 0.8 Why Wrapper-Only Was Correct

v0.5.40 chose a wrapper-only Comms rung because:

    Cypher now has schema, DB helpers, HTTP routes, and scoped envelope routes;
    Comms needed a typed client bridge before app/runtime wiring;
    exposing a typed wrapper lets future relay bridge or app code target Relay Space routes without embedding raw paths everywhere;
    keeping wrapper work out of app/runtime avoids premature provider live-flow and OpenMLS join claims;
    tests can confirm request/response contracts without starting real Cypher;
    no trust state or identity candidate mutation is needed for a client wrapper.

### 0.5 HTTP Routes Implemented

`POST /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/envelopes`:

    confirms the Relay Space exists first;
    accepts sender_device_id;
    accepts recipient_device_id;
    accepts content_type;
    accepts protocol_version;
    accepts ciphertext_b64;
    accepts client_created_at;
    validates required envelope fields;
    validates supported content type;
    validates supported protocol version for content type;
    enforces the Phase 1 ciphertext_b64 size limit;
    validates ciphertext_b64 base64 decoding;
    computes payload_sha256 and payload_size_bytes;
    verifies sender and recipient devices exist;
    inserts envelopes row with relay_space_id populated;
    returns envelope_id, relay_space_id, delivery_state, server_received_at, payload_sha256, and payload_size_bytes.

`GET /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/devices/{device_id}/envelopes`:

    confirms the Relay Space exists first;
    confirms the recipient device exists;
    returns queued envelopes where relay_space_id and recipient_device_id match;
    excludes unscoped envelopes;
    excludes envelopes scoped to other Relay Spaces;
    returns relay_space_id, device_id, and envelopes list.

`POST /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/envelopes/{envelope_id}/ack`:

    confirms the Relay Space exists first;
    requires recipient_device_id;
    loads the envelope by envelope_id;
    checks that envelope.relay_space_id matches the path relay_space_id;
    checks that recipient_device_id matches the envelope recipient;
    returns envelope_not_found if the envelope does not exist or is not in that Relay Space;
    returns recipient_mismatch for wrong recipient;
    preserves idempotent ack response when already acknowledged;
    inserts an envelope_acks row when needed;
    updates the matching scoped envelope to acknowledged;
    returns envelope_id, relay_space_id, delivery_state, and acknowledged_at.

v0.5.39 continues the routing-only substrate boundary.

    content_type;
    protocol_version;
    ciphertext_b64;
    payload_sha256;
    payload_size_bytes;
    delivery_state;
    acknowledged_at.

The scoped envelope layer does not introduce response fields or route names implying:

    verified identity;
    trust authority;
    local verification;
    key replacement;
    provider safety truth;
    plaintext authority;
    Comms trust.json authority;
    Comms identity-candidates.json authority.

The route stores ciphertext only and does not claim plaintext access or local verification.

### 0.8 Why Separate Scoped Routes Were Correct

The v0.5.39 preflight asked whether to extend existing `/v0/envelopes` and `/v0/devices/{device_id}/envelopes` with optional `relay_space_id`, or to add separate Relay Space-scoped routes.

Separate scoped routes were selected because:

    existing unscoped routes already represent direct device-to-device queue semantics;
    Relay Space introduces a routing/conversation container;
    optional relay_space_id on existing routes could blur queue semantics;
    explicit scoped paths make future Comms wrapper behavior easier to reason about;
    route names make the Relay Space context visible in submit, inbox, and ack;
    wrong-space ack can cleanly return envelope_not_found instead of leaking cross-space membership;
    implementation remains additive instead of mutating existing route semantics.

### 0.5 HTTP Routes Implemented

`POST /v0/relay-spaces`:

    accepts optional relay_space_id;
    accepts display_label;
    accepts created_by_account_id;
    accepts created_by_device_id;
    calls CreateRelaySpace;
    returns 201 with RelaySpace JSON.

`GET /v0/relay-spaces`:

    calls ListRelaySpaces;
    returns relay_spaces list.

`GET /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}`:

    calls GetRelaySpace;
    returns 404 relay_space_not_found when absent;
    returns RelaySpace JSON when present.

`POST /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/invites`:

    confirms the Relay Space exists first;
    accepts optional relay_space_invite_id;
    accepts invite_token or invite_token_hash;
    generates invite_token when both invite_token and invite_token_hash are omitted;
    accepts/generates display_code;
    accepts word_code;
    accepts created_by_member_id;
    accepts expires_at;
    accepts max_claims;
    accepts state;
    accepts note;
    calls CreateRelaySpaceInvite;
    returns 201 with relay_space_invite and invite_token.

`POST /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/members`:

    confirms the Relay Space exists first;
    requires account_id;
    accepts optional routing_member_id;
    accepts optional device_id;
    accepts display_label;
    accepts state;
    accepts last_seen_at;
    calls RegisterRelaySpaceMember;
    returns 201 with RelaySpaceMember JSON.

`GET /v0/relay-spaces/{relay_space_id}/members`:

    confirms the Relay Space exists first;
    calls ListRelaySpaceMembers;
    returns relay_space_id and members list.

### 0.6 Routing-Only Boundary Preserved

v0.5.38 continues the routing-only substrate boundary.

HTTP route names and response fields use:

    relay_space;
    relay_space_invite;
    routing_member;
    member;
    display_code;
    word_code;
    invite_token_hash.

The HTTP route layer does not introduce response fields or route names implying:

    verified identity;
    trust authority;
    local verification;
    key replacement;
    provider safety truth;
    plaintext authority;
    Comms trust.json authority;
    Comms identity-candidates.json authority.

`TestRelaySpaceHTTPDoesNotExposeTrustOrVerifiedFields` explicitly checks the Relay Space HTTP response for `trust` and `verified` strings.

### 0.5 DB Helpers Implemented

`CreateRelaySpace`:

    trims input fields;
    generates relay_space_id if omitted;
    sets created_at to NowUTC() if omitted;
    inserts relay_spaces row;
    returns GetRelaySpace result.

`GetRelaySpace`:

    returns a RelaySpace by relay_space_id;
    maps NULL creator/disabled fields to empty strings;
    returns ErrRelaySpaceNotFound for missing/blank IDs.

`ListRelaySpaces`:

    lists relay spaces ordered by created_at then relay_space_id;
    maps nullable creator/disabled fields to empty strings.

`CreateRelaySpaceInvite`:

    trims input fields;
    generates relay_space_invite_id if omitted;
    requires relay_space_id;
    accepts invite_token_hash directly or hashes invite_token with HashInviteCode;
    requires display_code;
    sets created_at to NowUTC() if omitted;
    defaults state to active if omitted;
    supports word_code, created_by_member_id, expires_at, max_claims, and note;
    returns GetRelaySpaceInviteByTokenHash result.

`GetRelaySpaceInviteByTokenHash`:

    returns a RelaySpaceInvite by invite_token_hash;
    maps nullable word_code, created_by_member_id, expires_at, max_claims, and note;
    returns ErrRelaySpaceInviteNotFound for missing/blank token hashes.

`RegisterRelaySpaceMember`:

    trims input fields;
    generates routing_member_id if omitted;
    requires relay_space_id;
    requires account_id;
    defaults state to active if omitted;
    defaults joined_at to NowUTC() if omitted;
    inserts relay_space_members row;
    returns GetRelaySpaceMember result.

`GetRelaySpaceMember`:

    returns a RelaySpaceMember by routing_member_id;
    maps nullable device_id, last_seen_at, and disabled_at to empty strings;
    returns ErrRelaySpaceMemberNotFound for missing/blank IDs.

`ListRelaySpaceMembers`:

    requires relay_space_id;
    lists routing members ordered by joined_at then routing_member_id;
    maps nullable device_id, last_seen_at, and disabled_at to empty strings.

### 0.6 Routing-Only Boundary Preserved

v0.5.37 continues the v0.5.36 routing-only substrate boundary.

Helper names and types use:

    RelaySpace;
    RelaySpaceInvite;
    RelaySpaceMember;
    RoutingMemberID;
    CreateRelaySpace;
    CreateRelaySpaceInvite;
    RegisterRelaySpaceMember;
    ListRelaySpaceMembers.

The helper layer does not introduce names or fields implying:

    verified identity;
    trust authority;
    local verification;
    key replacement;
    provider safety truth;
    plaintext authority;
    Comms trust.json authority;
    Comms identity-candidates.json authority.

`TestRelaySpaceHelpersPreserveRoutingOnlyNamingBoundary` explicitly rejects helper names containing `verified` or `trust`.

### 0.7 Scope Preserved

v0.5.37 does not:

    add Relay Space HTTP API routes;
    add create/get/list HTTP endpoints;
    add invite create/claim HTTP endpoints;
    add routing member registration/list HTTP endpoints;
    add Relay Space-scoped envelope API behavior;
    change Cypher runtime route behavior;
    change Comms runtime behavior;
    add Comms Relay Space client wrappers;
    wire provider live-flow;
    automate OpenMLS join;
    add local-backbone validation profile;
    add CLI/registry entries;
    implement full local-backbone;
    implement destructive reset/recovery/re-enrollment;
    implement vault/PQ/hybrid;
    make production/security/audit claims.

### 0.8 Why DB Helpers Before HTTP API Was Correct

v0.5.36 left a schema substrate but no typed store helpers.

v0.5.37 chose DB helpers before HTTP API because:

    helper methods isolate database behavior before external route shapes are committed;
    helper tests can enforce routing-only semantics cheaply;
    future HTTP handlers can call typed methods rather than embedding more SQL in route handlers;
    it avoids exposing external API contracts before the data behavior is stable;
    it keeps the implementation claim small and testable.

### 0.5 Schema Implemented

The new schema substrate is intentionally minimal and routing-only.

`relay_spaces`:

    relay_space_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY
    display_label TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
    created_by_account_id TEXT
    created_by_device_id TEXT
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
    disabled_at TEXT
    FOREIGN KEY(created_by_account_id) REFERENCES accounts(account_id)
    FOREIGN KEY(created_by_device_id) REFERENCES devices(device_id)

`relay_space_members`:

    routing_member_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY
    relay_space_id TEXT NOT NULL
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL
    device_id TEXT
    display_label TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
    state TEXT NOT NULL
    joined_at TEXT NOT NULL
    last_seen_at TEXT
    disabled_at TEXT
    FOREIGN KEY(relay_space_id) REFERENCES relay_spaces(relay_space_id)
    FOREIGN KEY(account_id) REFERENCES accounts(account_id)
    FOREIGN KEY(device_id) REFERENCES devices(device_id)
    CHECK(state IN ('active', 'disabled', 'left'))

`relay_space_invites`:

    relay_space_invite_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY
    relay_space_id TEXT NOT NULL
    invite_token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
    display_code TEXT NOT NULL
    word_code TEXT
    created_by_member_id TEXT
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
    expires_at TEXT
    max_claims INTEGER
    claim_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
    state TEXT NOT NULL
    note TEXT
    FOREIGN KEY(relay_space_id) REFERENCES relay_spaces(relay_space_id)
    FOREIGN KEY(created_by_member_id) REFERENCES relay_space_members(routing_member_id)
    CHECK(state IN ('active', 'claimed', 'disabled', 'expired'))
    CHECK(max_claims IS NULL OR max_claims >= 1)
    CHECK(claim_count >= 0)

`envelopes`:

    relay_space_id TEXT REFERENCES relay_spaces(relay_space_id)

### 0.6 Routing-Only Boundary Preserved

The v0.5.36 schema does not include:

    trust state;
    verified identity;
    local verification result;
    candidate identity authority;
    provider safety truth;
    key replacement authority;
    plaintext authority;
    Comms trust.json authority;
    Comms identity-candidates.json authority.

The tests explicitly reject the idea that routing-member state can be `verified`.

The schema uses the term `routing_member_id`, matching the v0.5.31 member terminology boundary:

    routing_member = server-side routing/access state;
    provider_member = OpenMLS/provider cryptographic group membership;
    local_verified_device = Comms-local trust result.

### 0.5 Conditional GO Meaning

Conditional GO means:

    the planning chain is coherent enough to plan the first narrow implementation rung;
    the first implementation rung can be scoped to routing/storage substrate;
    the project can stop adding broad preconditions before any code;
    implementation can proceed later only with strict continuity and boundary checks.

Conditional GO does not mean:

    full local-backbone is ready;
    local-backbone validation exists;
    Relay Space is implemented;
    provider live-flow is implemented;
    OpenMLS join is automated;
    local trust is mature;
    CLI/registry can be exposed;
    production/security claims are allowed.

### 0.6 Current Readiness Chain

Recent controlling chain:

    v0.5.30:
      local-backbone closer but still blocked; selected Relay Space recon/planning.

    v0.5.31:
      Relay Space join/invite/member mechanics planned.

    v0.5.32:
      provider/OpenMLS live-flow boundary planned; broad provider live-flow deferred until Relay Space schema/API and validation boundaries exist.

    v0.5.33:
      validation-profile boundary planned; local-backbone validation profile deferred; generated-state cleanup and release-package/live-umbrella boundaries preserved.

v0.5.34 concludes that the next useful movement is not more broad planning before code, but a cleanup/readiness checkpoint followed by a narrow Cypher Relay Space substrate implementation if still claim-safe.

### 0.7 Why Not Full Local-backbone

Full local-backbone remains blocked because:

    Relay Space schema/API does not exist;
    Relay Space implementation does not exist;
    Relay Space-scoped envelopes do not exist;
    provider live-flow is not wired;
    Comms client wrappers for Relay Space do not exist;
    local-backbone validation profile does not exist;
    mature verification ceremony does not exist;
    destructive recovery/reset/re-enrollment remains intentionally absent;
    CLI/registry exposure would still overstate maturity;
    release-package local-backbone validation is not possible.

Therefore:

    do not call the next implementation local-backbone;
    call it a first narrow Relay Space substrate implementation.

### 0.8 First Implementation Target

Preferred first implementation target:

    Cypher Relay Space schema/API substrate.

Reason:

    provider live-flow needs routable Relay Space artifacts;
    Comms client wrappers need server/API substrate;
    local-backbone validation needs something concrete to validate;
    Relay Space must remain routing/storage only;
    Cypher can implement routing substrate without becoming trust authority.

Candidate first implementation surfaces:

    relay_spaces table;
    relay_space_invites table;
    relay_space_members table;
    relay_space_id-scoped envelope support or migration path;
    create/get/list Relay Space APIs;
    invite create/claim APIs;
    routing member registration/list APIs;
    tests proving routing-only semantics;
    tests proving no trust authority is introduced.

Do not implement all of this at once if a smaller schema-only rung is safer.

### 0.9 Still Deferred

Defer:

    Comms broad provider live-flow;
    provider event broad import;
    automatic candidate promotion;
    trust.json mutation from provider observation;
    Relay Space membership as trust;
    OpenMLS/provider membership as local verification;
    local-backbone validation profile;
    CLI/registry exposure;
    destructive reset/recovery/re-enrollment helpers;
    vault;
    PQ/hybrid;
    hostile-server harnesses;
    deployability claims.

### 0.10 Cypher Boundary for First Implementation

Cypher may implement routing/storage substrate.

Cypher may store:

    relay_space_id;
    invite metadata;
    routing_member records;
    routing account/device labels;
    envelope routing metadata;
    ack state;
    payload size/hash metadata;
    timestamps and operational routing fields.

Cypher must not store or claim:

    verified trust;
    local trust state;
    plaintext;
    local verification result;
    key replacement authority;
    provider safety truth;
    trust.json authority;
    identity-candidates.json authority.

### 0.11 Comms Boundary After First Implementation

Comms should not be broadly wired immediately after Cypher schema/API lands.

Later Comms work should be split into:

    Relay Space client wrapper;
    no-trust-mutation tests;
    candidate handoff only when identity material is explicit;
    provider/OpenMLS join wiring;
    ack-boundary tests;
    validation profile integration.

Relay Space server state should enter Comms as routing context, not trust truth.

### 0.12 Validation Boundary After v0.5.34

Do not add local-backbone validation profile in v0.5.34.

Future validation profile work should happen only after concrete substrate exists.

A future profile may prove:

    local Cypher starts;
    Relay Space schema exists;
    Relay Space can be created;
    invite can be created/claimed;
    routing member can be registered;
    Relay Space-scoped envelope can be stored/retrieved;
    no trust authority is created by routing operations.

It must not prove:

    production secure messaging;
    hostile-server safety;
    metadata privacy;
    mature verification UX;
    provider live-flow correctness;
    local verified trust;
    deployment readiness;
    external audit/certification.

## 0. v0.5.33 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.33 is a docs-only validation-profile boundary planning rung following the v0.5.32 provider/OpenMLS live-flow boundary plan.

v0.5.32 established:

    broad provider live-flow remains deferred;
    provider live-flow depends on Relay Space schema/API substrate;
    future wiring must preserve candidate/review/recovery/trust boundaries;
    provider observation must not verify identity;
    provider observation must not mutate trust.json by itself;
    ack remains sidecar-open/consume gated;
    v0.5.33 should define validation-profile boundaries before local-backbone-style implementation.

v0.5.33 applies that doctrine to validation profiles and generated-state safety.

Decision:

    no validation profile implementation yet;
    no local-backbone validation profile yet;
    live-git umbrella validation and release-package validation must stay distinct;
    generated state and cleanup boundaries must be explicit;
    future local-backbone validation must define exactly what it proves and does not prove;
    trust/candidate/provider/generated state must not be destructively cleaned without narrow rules;
    CLI/registry remains deferred;
    v0.5.34 should be local-backbone go/no-go reassessment.

New committed docs:

    carbonstack/docs/187-v0.5.33-validation-profile-boundary-v0.md
    carbonstack-comms/docs/21-validation-profile-boundary-v0.md
    carbonstack-cypher/docs/validation-profile-boundary-v0.md

Updated docs/index/README surfaces:

    carbonstack/docs/README.md
    carbonstack-comms/README.md
    carbonstack-cypher/README.md

This rung does not add code, validation profiles, registry entries, CLI surfaces, schema/API, or runtime behavior.

### 0.5 Existing Validation Profile Context

Current runner/profile surfaces include:

    doctor;
    core;
    local-cypher;
    dev-runtime-openmls;
    dev-runtime-openmls-wrappers;
    full;
    release-snapshot;
    write-checksums;
    verify-checksums.

Important current boundaries preserved by v0.5.33:

    dev-runtime-openmls is live-umbrella only;
    dev-runtime-openmls-wrappers is live-umbrella only;
    release-snapshot is package-root oriented;
    full runs release-snapshot then local-cypher;
    clean-generated is explicit opt-in;
    artifact scans are non-destructive unless clean-generated is requested.

Do not collapse these into a premature local-backbone profile.

### 0.6 Release Package vs Live Umbrella Distinction

Release-package validation may prove:

    package layout exists;
    required docs/files exist;
    checksums match;
    strict pre-test artifact scan passes;
    package-root core validation passes;
    release snapshot can be validated from a fresh extracted/staged root.

Release-package validation must not claim:

    local-backbone works;
    live Relay Space works;
    provider live-flow works;
    deployment works;
    hostile-server safety;
    production security;
    metadata privacy;
    mature UX;
    certification.

Live-umbrella validation may prove:

    sibling git checkout layout exists;
    live dev scripts exist;
    Cypher can run locally;
    OpenMLS dev runtime smoke proof can run;
    wrapper-based OpenMLS dev smoke proof can run;
    package tests pass across current working repos.

Live-umbrella validation must not claim:

    release package reproducibility;
    deployability;
    production readiness;
    hostile-server safety;
    security certification.

### 0.7 Future Local-backbone Validation Boundary

Future local-backbone validation may eventually prove a narrow dev path such as:

    Cypher local server starts;
    Relay Space schema/API exists;
    Relay Space can be created;
    invite can be created and claimed;
    routing member can be registered;
    Relay Space-scoped envelope can be submitted and retrieved;
    provider/OpenMLS lifecycle can run through explicit dev paths;
    candidate identity material can be observed without verification;
    trust/recovery boundaries are preserved;
    ack remains sidecar-open/consume gated;
    generated state remains inside known generated roots.

It may only prove this if the corresponding implementation exists.

Even if future local-backbone validation passes, it must not claim:

    production secure messaging;
    hostile-server safety;
    metadata privacy;
    external audit;
    certification;
    mature verification UX;
    general-public usability;
    deployability;
    key-compromise recovery correctness;
    PQ/hybrid security;
    vault security;
    server trustworthiness;
    verified identity import from provider observation;
    local trust from Relay Space membership;
    local trust from OpenMLS/provider membership.

Passing validation is a development proof, not a security certification.

### 0.8 Generated State and Cleanup Boundary

Future profiles must explicitly classify generated state.

Known generated/build roots may include:

    OpenMLS sidecar target;
    OpenMLS sidecar .carbonstack-openmls-sidecar-state;
    temporary local Cypher DBs;
    local runner temp directories;
    release/checksum artifacts;
    provider-storage.json;
    signer.json;
    Go cache/temp roots.

Trust-sensitive state may include:

    trust.json;
    trust-events.jsonl;
    identity-candidates.json;
    provider identity state;
    provider storage/checkpoint state;
    sidecar signer state.

Cleanup must distinguish:

    build artifacts;
    dev fixture artifacts;
    temporary runner artifacts;
    trust-bearing state;
    identity-bearing state;
    recovery-relevant state.

Allowed cleanup class:

    known generated/build roots created by the validation profile;
    temporary local test DBs under runner-owned temp directories;
    known OpenMLS sidecar generated roots when explicitly requested.

Disallowed cleanup class unless a future destructive/reset design exists:

    user trust.json;
    user trust-events.jsonl;
    user identity-candidates.json;
    user provider identity state;
    user provider storage/checkpoint state;
    non-temp Cypher DBs;
    unknown DBs;
    unknown .carbonstack-* directories;
    repo docs/source files;
    release artifacts not created by the running profile.

Rule:

    validation cleanup must not become recovery/reset.

### 0.9 Trust / Identity / Candidate / Provider Boundaries

Validation profiles must not mutate trust semantics unless the profile explicitly exists to test such mutation and the test state is isolated.

Default validation must not:

    verify devices;
    mark devices changed;
    revoke devices;
    promote candidate identities;
    replace keys;
    suppress reverify warnings;
    bypass candidate review;
    bypass recovery classification.

Test-only isolated trust stores may be used only under temp directories or explicitly generated roots.

Comms-specific rule:

    provider observation is not verification;
    Relay Space routing membership is not local trust;
    OpenMLS/provider membership is not local verification;
    recovery classification is not recovery execution;
    identity-candidates.json must not mutate from Relay Space routing membership alone;
    trust.json must not mutate from provider observation alone.

Cypher-specific rule:

    Cypher validation may prove routing/storage behavior;
    Cypher validation must not prove verified identity, local trust, OpenMLS group safety, hostile-server safety, metadata privacy, production deployment readiness, or server trustworthiness.

### 0.10 Ack Boundary

Future validation profiles must preserve ack-after-open:

    Relay Space routing membership is not enough;
    invite claim is not enough;
    envelope retrieval is not enough;
    artifact write is not enough;
    provider report generation is not enough;
    trust-history append is not enough;
    candidate observation is not enough;
    recovery classification is not enough;
    only successful sidecar message-open/consume may permit ack unless a later negative-ack/quarantine design is explicitly created.

A future validation profile may test this boundary, but must not weaken it.

### 0.11 Registry / CLI Boundary

Do not add CLI or registry entries yet for:

    Relay Space;
    local-backbone;
    provider live-flow;
    recovery execution;
    destructive reset;
    re-enrollment;
    vault;
    PQ/hybrid.

Registry/CLI entries should wait until:

    implementation exists;
    validation boundary exists;
    generated-state cleanup is clear;
    claim wording is honest;
    commands are useful as a supported dev surface.

Existing registry entries may continue to document current dev/runtime surfaces.

### 0.12 Future Profile Shape

Future validation work should be split rather than bundled.

Possible future profiles:

    relay-space-schema-dev;
    relay-space-api-dev;
    relay-space-routing-dev;
    provider-join-dev;
    local-backbone-dev;
    local-backbone-cleanup-dev;
    release-local-backbone-snapshot only much later if package-safe.

Do not create all of these at once.

The first future implementation should likely be Cypher Relay Space schema/API before broad Comms provider live-flow.

### 0.13 Recommended Next Rungs

Recommended sequence after v0.5.33:

    v0.5.34 local-backbone go/no-go reassessment;
    v0.5.35 cleanup / roadmap refresh / possible dev-only CLI-registry prep;
    v0.5.36+ first narrow implementation if claim-safe, likely Cypher Relay Space schema/API before Comms broad provider live-flow.

If local-backbone is not claim-safe at v0.5.34, continue planning or cleanup rather than forcing implementation.

### 0.14 Boundary Preserved

v0.5.33 does not:

    implement new validation profiles;
    implement local-backbone validation;
    implement Relay Space schema;
    implement Relay Space API;
    implement Relay Space join;
    wire provider live-flow;
    add Cypher schema changes;
    add Comms client wrapper changes;
    add CLI/registry entries;
    execute destructive reset/recovery;
    implement backup/restore;
    implement re-enrollment mutation;
    mutate trust.json;
    mutate identity-candidates.json;
    replace key material;
    verify identity;
    change send/open/ack behavior;
    implement vault;
    implement PQ/hybrid crypto;
    change CarbonStackOS.

### 0.15 Significance

v0.5.33 prevents a premature jump from provider live-flow boundary planning to a validation profile that would overclaim local-backbone readiness.

It locks in that validation is not certification, cleanup is not recovery, live-umbrella and release-package validation must remain distinct, and future local-backbone validation must be scoped to implemented substrate and explicit nonclaims.

This also sets up v0.5.34 as a meaningful go/no-go reassessment instead of a vague “are we ready yet?” checkpoint.

### 0.16 Do Not Do Next

Do not:

    implement a local-backbone validation profile immediately;
    implement Relay Space schema/API without v0.5.34 go/no-go;
    expose CLI/registry yet;
    collapse live-umbrella validation into release-package validation;
    use validation success as a production/security claim;
    clean trust-bearing or identity-bearing state destructively;
    treat cleanup as recovery/reset;
    mutate trust.json from provider observation;
    mutate identity-candidates.json from routing membership alone;
    treat Cypher routing membership, Relay Space membership, invite claim, QR scan, or OpenMLS/provider membership as local verification;
    ack before successful sidecar message-open/consume;
    implement destructive reset/recovery/re-enrollment helpers;
    implement vault/PQ/hybrid now;
    claim metadata privacy;
    claim hostile-server safety;
    claim production readiness;
    commit raw LogDoc or breakpoint files to Gitea.

v0.5.33 does not claim:

    Relay Space is a routable server/conversation container and vector to OpenMLS join;
    OpenMLS/provider join is cryptographic group participation;
    local Comms verification is actual trust/auth/presence;
    Cypher may store routing membership but must not become identity authority;
    Comms remains local trust/candidate/recovery authority;

    provider observation must not verify identity;
    provider observation must not mutate trust.json by itself;
    ack must remain sidecar-open/consume gated;
    v0.5.33 should be validation profile boundary planning.

### 0.5 v0.5.32 Provider Live-flow Model

Provider live-flow means runtime wiring between Comms application/client flows and OpenMLS/provider sidecar operations.

Relevant provider operations include:

    identity create/load/status;
    public bundle / KeyPackage export;
    conversation/group create;
    member add;
    Welcome creation;
    Welcome consume/join;
    message protect;
    message open;
    storage/checkpoint behavior;
    provider event/report emission;
    provider trust classification;
    candidate identity observation;
    trust-history append where explicitly safe.

Current dev surfaces prove pieces of the OpenMLS lifecycle, but they are not mature provider live-flow and do not imply local-backbone readiness.

### 0.6 Why Broad Provider Live-flow Is Still Deferred

Broad provider live-flow wiring remains premature because:

    Relay Space schema/API does not exist;
    Relay Space join/invite/member implementation does not exist;
    routing membership is not yet represented as a first-class server substrate;
    validation profile claims are not defined;
    cleanup/reset boundaries for generated provider state are not mature enough;
    provider observations still must not verify identity;
    send/open/ack behavior must not be weakened;
    mature verification UX does not exist;
    CLI/registry exposure would overstate maturity.

Do not implement next:

    broad provider event import;
    automatic candidate promotion;
    automatic trust.json mutation;
    automatic local-backbone profile;
    automatic Relay Space join;
    automatic OpenMLS group trust.

### 0.7 Smallest Safe Future Wiring Shape

Preferred future order:

    Cypher Relay Space schema/API substrate;
    Comms client wrappers for Relay Space APIs;
    provider/OpenMLS join wiring against explicit Relay Space artifacts;
    candidate observation handoff only when identity material is actually present;
    recovery/trust safety checks before trust-sensitive operations;
    validation-profile planning and implementation only when claim-safe.

A safe provider live-flow may eventually:

    call sidecar operations;
    produce provider events;
    build provider trust reports;
    build provider trust-history/event drafts;
    append explicitly selected trust-history events;
    observe candidate identity material;
    classify mapped mismatch;
    classify recovery state;
    block or warn on unsafe state;
    preserve ack-after-open.

A safe provider live-flow must not:

    mark identity verified;
    mutate trust.json from provider observation alone;
    silently replace known key material;
    bypass candidate review;
    bypass recovery classification;
    weaken send/open/ack behavior;
    trust Cypher routing membership as identity;
    trust Relay Space membership as identity;
    treat provider membership as local verification.

### 0.8 Relay Space / Cypher Dependency

Provider live-flow should wait for Relay Space schema/API substrate because provider join needs to be anchored to routable server/conversation mechanics.

Future Relay Space implementation should likely provide:

    relay_spaces table;
    relay_space_invites table;
    relay_space_members table;
    relay_space_id-scoped envelope routing;
    create/list/get Relay Space APIs;
    invite create/claim APIs;
    routing member registration/list APIs;
    Relay Space-scoped envelope submit/retrieve/ack APIs.

These are routing primitives only.

They must not create verified trust.

Cypher may eventually store and route Relay Space-scoped artifacts, but must not provide:

    verified identity;
    local trust state;
    provider safety truth;
    local verification result;
    key replacement authority;
    trust.json mutation authority.

### 0.9 Candidate / Mismatch / Recovery Handoff

Provider-observed identity material should enter candidate and review flows.

It may become:

    candidate identity;
    continuity observation;
    review-required conflict;
    reverify-required state;
    changed-candidate state;
    revoked/compromised block.

It must not become verified trust without local verification.

Provider live-flow must account for recovery state.

Unsafe recovery classifications should block or warn before trust-sensitive operations:

    missing trust store:
      do not claim continuity or verified trust.

    corrupt trust store:
      block trust-sensitive promotion and trusted send/open paths.

    requires reverify:
      allow candidate observation and diagnostics, but block trusted promotion.

    blocked revoked or compromised:
      block promotion and trusted send.

Recovery-history append is not recovery execution.
Recovery orchestration is not destructive reset.

### 0.10 Ack Boundary

Ack remains sidecar-open/consume gated.

Not enough:

    Relay Space routing membership;
    invite claim;
    envelope retrieval;
    artifact write;
    provider report;
    trust-history append;
    candidate observation;
    recovery classification.

Only successful sidecar message-open/consume may permit ack unless a later negative-ack/quarantine design is explicitly created.

v0.5.32 does not create negative ack.

### 0.11 Validation / CLI / Registry Implications

v0.5.33 should define validation profile boundaries before any local-backbone-style implementation.

A future profile must answer:

    what is proved;
    what is not proved;
    whether it requires live git umbrella;
    whether it can run from release packages;
    what generated state it creates;
    what cleanup is safe;
    what trust/candidate/provider state it touches;
    what claims are forbidden even when it passes.

Do not add a local-backbone profile in v0.5.32.

Do not add CLI or registry entries yet.

Existing dev commands may remain documented, but provider live-flow / Relay Space / local-backbone command exposure should wait until:

    Relay Space schema/API exists;
    validation profile boundary exists;
    local-backbone go/no-go is complete;
    command semantics are honest;
    cleanup/reset safety is clear.

### 0.12 Recommended Next Rungs

Recommended sequence after v0.5.32:

    v0.5.33 validation profile boundary planning;

    v0.5.35 cleanup / roadmap refresh / possible dev-only CLI-registry prep;
    v0.5.36+ first narrow implementation if claim-safe, likely Cypher Relay Space schema/API before Comms broad provider live-flow.

If implementation begins later, split it into:

    Cypher Relay Space schema-only spike;
    Cypher Relay Space API spike;
    Comms Relay Space client wrapper spike;
    Comms no-trust-mutation tests;
    provider/OpenMLS join wiring spike;
    validation profile spike.

### 0.13 Boundary Preserved

v0.5.32 does not:

### 0.5 v0.5.31 Relay Space Model

Core model:

    Relay Space = addressable routing/conversation container.
    Invite = authorization to attempt routing access / join flow.
    Join = staged process, not atomic trust.
    Member = context-specific word; must be qualified.
    OpenMLS/provider membership = cryptographic group state.
    Local verified trust = Comms-local trust/auth/presence decision.

Do not collapse:

    joined Relay Space;
    OpenMLS group member;
    locally verified/trusted participant.

The guiding distinction is:

    Relay Space is a vector to OpenMLS join.
    OpenMLS join is cryptographic group participation.
    Local verification is actual trust/auth/presence.

### 0.6 Addressing / Invite / QR / Word-Code Decision

Canonical Relay Space identifier:

    UUIDv4, 128-bit random token, or equivalent high-entropy opaque ID.

Do not use a 12-hex-character value as the canonical Relay Space ID.

Reason:

    12 hex characters are 48 bits.
    That may be acceptable as a human display code, but not as a canonical globally exposed identifier.

Human display code:

    12 to 16 hex characters;
    grouped for readability, such as 8F3A-C91B-2D44;
    optional word-code phrase derived from canonical invite token or short display code.

Word-code phrase:

    Example shape: banana-wall-red-applesauce.
    Useful for verbal comparison / anti-typo confirmation.
    Not proof of trust by itself.

QR code:

    should encode the full invite package/token/URL;
    should not encode only the short display code.

Possible future QR package fields:

    server URL;
    relay_space_id;
    invite token;
    invite display code;
    optional relay_space label;
    protocol version;
    expiry/constraints if implemented;
    maybe provider bootstrap hint later;
    checksum/digest.

QR scan still must not imply verified trust.

### 0.7 Join Lifecycle Decision

Join should be staged:

    invite_created
    invite_claimed
    routing_member_registered
    provider_keypackage_submitted_or_observed
    provider_welcome_created
    provider_welcome_consumed
    provider_joined
    candidate_identity_observed
    candidate_review_required
    locally_verified

Meanings:

    invite_claimed:
      Cypher accepted invite/routing credential.

    routing_member_registered:
      Cypher can route envelopes for the member/device.

    provider_keypackage_submitted_or_observed:
      Comms/OpenMLS material needed for group join became available.

    provider_welcome_created:
      existing participant created provider/OpenMLS Welcome.

    provider_welcome_consumed:
      joining participant consumed Welcome.

    provider_joined:
      provider/OpenMLS state says the device is cryptographically in the group.

    candidate_identity_observed:
      Comms observed identity material and stores candidate/unverified state.

    candidate_review_required:
      Comms detected unverified/conflicting/reverify-required state.

    locally_verified:
      local verification ceremony or explicit trust decision completed later.

Only `locally_verified` should mean trusted.

### 0.8 Qualified Member Terminology

The word `member` is overloaded and must be qualified.

Required terms:

    routing_member
    provider_member
    local_known_device
    local_verified_device
    candidate_identity
    blocked_or_revoked_device

Definitions:

    routing_member:
      server-side access/routing state in Cypher.
      Can route envelopes.
      Not trusted identity.

    provider_member:
      cryptographic group membership according to OpenMLS/provider state.
      Not automatically locally verified.

    local_verified_device:
      Comms-local trust-state result.
      Must not be assigned by Cypher or by provider observation alone.

### 0.9 Cypher Responsibility Model

Cypher may store:

    relay_space_id;
    routing_member_id;
    account_id or routing account label;
    device_id;
    invite claim metadata;
    envelope queues scoped to relay_space_id;
    ack state;
    timing;
    payload size/hash metadata;
    access/rate-limit state;
    operational retention metadata.

Cypher may eventually expose:

    create Relay Space;
    create invite;
    claim invite;
    register routing member/device;
    submit envelope scoped to relay_space_id;
    list/retrieve envelopes for a routing member/device;
    ack envelope after Comms permits ack;
    list routing metadata as allowed by local dev API.

Cypher must not store/claim:

    verified trust;
    local trust state;
    plaintext;
    trust.json authority;
    verification ceremony result;
    key replacement authority;
    provider safety truth;
    locally authenticated presence.

### 0.10 Comms and OpenMLS Responsibility Model

Comms owns:

    local identity state;
    local trust state;
    local trust history;
    candidate identity storage/review;
    mapped mismatch classification;
    recovery classification/orchestration;
    provider event classification;
    provider trust reports/history;
    send/open/ack policy;
    future verification ceremony;
    local warnings/UX.

Comms must treat Relay Space artifacts as inputs to local policy, not as authoritative trust.

Relay Space join should feed:

    candidate observation;
    provider/OpenMLS join;
    local recovery checks;
    local review/reverify/verification path.

OpenMLS/provider owns cryptographic group operations:

    identity creation/loading;
    public bundle / KeyPackage generation;
    conversation/group creation;
    member add;
    Welcome generation;
    Welcome consume/join;
    message protect/open;
    storage/checkpoint state.

Provider/OpenMLS state can indicate cryptographic membership.

It cannot by itself decide local verified trust.

### 0.11 Recovery / Unsafe State / Ack / Metadata Boundaries

Relay Space actions must account for recovery safety.

Examples:

    recovery_missing_trust_store:
      do not claim trust continuity; allow only carefully bounded dev/routing diagnostics if needed.

    recovery_corrupt_trust_store:
      block trust-sensitive join/send/open/promotion flows.

    recovery_requires_reverify:
      allow candidate observation and routing diagnostics, but block trusted promotion.

    recovery_blocked_revoked:
      block promotion and trusted send.

    recovery_blocked_compromised:
      block promotion and trusted send.

Recovery history append is not recovery execution.

Ack boundary remains:

    server delivery is not enough;
    envelope retrieval is not enough;
    artifact write is not enough;
    provider report generation is not enough;
    trust-history append is not enough;
    event draft generation is not enough;
    routing membership is not enough;
    invite claim is not enough;
    only successful sidecar message-open/consume may permit ack unless a future negative-ack/quarantine design is explicitly created.

Relay Space does not provide metadata privacy.

Likely visible to Cypher later:

    Relay Space identifier;
    timing;
    envelope size;
    sender/recipient routing metadata;
    invite claim metadata;
    routing member/device records;
    ack timing;
    IP/network metadata unless hidden externally.

### 0.12 Future Implementation Guidance

Future implementation should be split.

Possible Cypher schema/API implementation rungs:

    Relay Space schema-only spike;
    Relay Space API-only spike;
    invite/claim mechanics;
    Relay Space-scoped envelopes;
    routing-member records;
    tests proving routing-only semantics.

Possible Comms integration rungs:

    client wrapper for Relay Space APIs;
    no trust mutation from routing membership;
    candidate handoff for observed identity material;
    provider/OpenMLS join wiring;
    tests proving no trust.json mutation from server membership;
    tests proving no identity-candidates.json mutation unless candidate observation is explicit;
    tests preserving ack boundary.

Do not combine Relay Space, provider live-flow, validation profile, CLI, and local-backbone into one rung.

### 0.13 Roadmap Refresh Decision

During Q/A, Relay Space practical mechanics proved more architecture-sensitive than expected.

Decision:

    refresh the roadmap PDF after this v0.5.31 breakpoint/logdoc is marked.

The refresh should:

    avoid production/security/audit claims.

This supersedes the prior v0.5.30 preference to wait until around v0.5.35, because the Relay Space mechanics plan materially changed the architecture picture and the user explicitly requested the earlier refresh.

### 0.14 Recommended Next Rungs

Recommended sequence after v0.5.31:

    roadmap PDF refresh at v0.5.31;
    v0.5.32 provider live-flow wiring boundary planning;
    v0.5.33 validation profile boundary planning;
    v0.5.34 local-backbone go/no-go reassessment;
    v0.5.35 cleanup / possible dev-only CLI-registry prep / roadmap refresh if needed;
    later Relay Space implementation only after schema/API boundary is stable.

If implementation pressure is high, split implementation into:

    Relay Space schema-only spike;
    Relay Space API-only spike;
    Comms client wrapper spike;
    OpenMLS join wiring spike;
    validation profile spike.

### 0.15 Boundary Preserved

v0.5.31 does not:

    implement Relay Space schema;
    implement Relay Space API;
    implement Relay Space join;
    implement invite mechanics;
    implement member tables;
    automate OpenMLS join;
    wire provider live-flow;
    change validation profiles;

    implement local-backbone;

### 0.16 Significance

v0.5.31 converts Relay Space from a high-level architectural concept into an implementation-shaping mechanics plan.

Most important preserved distinctions:

    routing membership is not trust;
    provider/OpenMLS membership is not local verification;
    local Comms verification is actual trust/auth/presence;
    Cypher routes/stores but does not decide trust;
    short display codes and word phrases are UX aids, not canonical security;
    QR is an invite package carrier, not a trust ceremony;
    unsafe recovery state must block/warn before trust-sensitive flows;
    ack remains successful-sidecar-open gated.

This makes future Relay Space implementation safer to plan, but it does not make Relay Space implemented or local-backbone ready.

        -> return structured result

v0.5.30 then reassessed whether that recovery work is enough to begin local-backbone implementation.

    local-backbone is closer, but still not implementation-ready.
    v0.5.31 should be a dedicated Relay Space recon/planning rung.

### 0.5 v0.5.30 Reassessment Details

v0.5.30 confirms that the v0.5.x trust/recovery arc has materially reduced the blocker set.

Implemented internal helper ladder now includes:

    provider trust report;
    provider trust history draft;
    provider trust event draft bridge;
    trust-owned provider append helper;
    candidate identity storage;
    mapped identity mismatch classifier;
    candidate review/update mechanics;
    candidate/mismatch history events;
    candidate observation orchestration;
    reset/recovery/re-enrollment boundary decision;
    pure recovery classifier;
    recovery-history append helpers;
    recovery orchestration / classification composition.

Meaning:

    Candidate identity is no longer only doctrine.
    Mapped provider identity mismatch is no longer only doctrine.
    Recovery is no longer only doctrine.
    Recovery classifications can be recorded in append-only history.
    Recovery orchestration can compose classification and optional history append.

Still true:

    helper orchestration is not user-facing recovery.
    local recovery-history append is not trust verification.
    provider observation is not identity verification.
    Relay Space membership will not equal trusted membership.
    Cypher is relay/storage context, not identity authority.

### 0.6 Why Local-backbone Is Closer

Local-backbone is materially closer than it was at v0.5.17 because these earlier blockers are now internal helper surfaces:

    candidate identity storage and dedupe;
    candidate state model;
    candidate review/update mechanics;
    candidate/mismatch history append;
    candidate observation orchestration;
    candidate-vs-known-device mismatch classifier;
    reset/recovery/re-enrollment boundary;
    recovery classifier;
    recovery-history append;
    recovery orchestration.

The remaining blocker set is now smaller and more nameable.

### 0.7 Why Local-backbone Is Still Blocked

Remaining blockers:

    Relay Space join/invite/member semantics are not planned deeply enough.
    Relay Space schema/API implementation does not exist.
    Provider live-flow wiring boundary is not decided.
    Broad provider event import is not wired into app flows.
    Comms send/inbox remain split between dev/runtime and older surfaces.
    Validation profile claim wording is not ready.
    Local-backbone cleanup/reset boundaries are not ready.
    CLI/registry surfaces would overstate maturity.
    Mature verification ceremony does not exist.
    Verified provider identity import remains forbidden.
    Destructive reset/recovery/re-enrollment mutation helpers do not exist and should not be rushed.
    Vault remains later.
    PQ/hybrid remains later.

### 0.8 Cypher Downstream Assessment

Cypher remains downstream relay/storage infrastructure.

Cypher currently provides useful downstream primitives:

    dev invite creation/claim surface;
    device registration/lookup;
    encrypted envelope submit/retrieve/ack;
    SQLite-backed local development persistence;
    local operator runbook;
    Relay Space boundary documentation.

Cypher must not become:

    identity authority;
    verified-device authority;
    trust root;
    plaintext authority;
    silent key-replacement authority;
    local trust-store mutation authority.

For v0.5.31, Cypher should be included as Relay Space downstream context but not as the place where trust semantics are decided.

### 0.9 v0.5.31 Relay Space Planning Target

Recommended next checkpoint:

    v0.5.31 Relay Space recon/planning

The rung should answer:

    what is a Relay Space?
    what is a join?
    what is an invite?
    what is a member?
    what is server-side membership?
    what is provider/MLS membership?
    what is local verified trust?
    what can Cypher store?
    what can Cypher claim?
    what must remain client-owned?
    what must fail loudly when identity/recovery state is unsafe?

v0.5.31 should not implement Relay Space.

Relay Space implementation should be a later separate rung only after the planning record stabilizes.

### 0.10 Provider Live-flow / Validation / CLI Decisions

Provider live-flow:

    Do not broadly wire provider live-flow next.
    Provider live-flow wiring depends on Relay Space membership semantics.
    Provider observations still must not verify identity.
    Provider event append must not mutate trust.json.
    Ack must remain open-success gated.
    Candidate/recovery helpers are still internal.

Validation profile:

    Do not add a local-backbone validation profile yet.
    Future local-backbone profile must clearly state what it proves and what it does not prove.
    It must distinguish live-git-umbrella-only work from release-package-validatable work.
    It must document generated state, cleanup behavior, trust/candidate/provider state touch points, and public package roots.

CLI/registry:

    Do not add CLI or registry entries yet.
    Recovery/reset/re-enrollment commands are dangerous.
    Relay Space is not planned deeply enough.
    Local-backbone is not claim-safe.
    Helper APIs are internal and not mature UX.

Roadmap:

    Do not refresh the roadmap PDF at v0.5.30.
    Preferred refresh timing is around v0.5.35, after Relay Space planning, provider live-flow boundary planning, validation-profile boundary planning, local-backbone go/no-go reassessment, and before CLI/registry prep if that becomes plausible.

### 0.11 Recommended Near-term Sequence

Recommended near-term sequence after v0.5.30:

    v0.5.31 Relay Space recon/planning;
    v0.5.32 provider live-flow wiring boundary;
    v0.5.33 validation profile boundary planning;
    v0.5.34 local-backbone go/no-go reassessment;
    v0.5.35 cleanup / possible dev-only CLI-registry prep / roadmap refresh.

Do not skip directly to local-backbone.

Do not implement Relay Space in the planning rung.

### 0.12 Boundary Preserved

v0.5.30 does not:

    implement local-backbone;
    implement Relay Space schema;
    implement Relay Space join/invite/member behavior;
    wire provider live-flow;
    change validation profiles;
    add CLI/registry entries;
    execute destructive reset/recovery;
    implement backup/restore;
    implement re-enrollment mutation;
    implement vault;
    implement PQ/hybrid crypto;
    change Comms code;
    change Cypher code;
    change CarbonStackOS.

v0.5.30 is the first post-recovery-orchestration blocker reassessment.

It prevents a premature jump from helper readiness to local-backbone claims.

It narrows the project’s next major embedded milestone to Relay Space planning, not implementation.

It also preserves the distinction between:

    server routing membership;
    provider/MLS membership;
    local candidate/trust state;
    verified device trust;
    recovery safety state.

This distinction is critical before any Relay Space or local-backbone claim becomes honest.
