## 0. v0.5.29 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.29 is an implementation rung following the v0.5.28 recovery-history append helper spike.

v0.5.28 made recovery classifications buildable as trust-history events and appendable through the existing provider append bridge. v0.5.29 composes that with the v0.5.26 classifier:

    classify recovery state
        -> optionally build recovery-history draft
        -> optionally append recovery-history event
        -> return structured orchestration result

New implementation:

    carbonstack-comms/internal/trust/identity_recovery_orchestration.go
    carbonstack-comms/internal/trust/identity_recovery_orchestration_test.go

Meaning:

    Comms can now run a non-destructive recovery orchestration helper.
    The helper reads/classifies local recovery state through ClassifyIdentityRecovery.
    The helper appends recovery-history events by default for non-clean recovery classifications.
    The helper skips recovery_clean_local_state history append by default to avoid trust-history noise.
    The helper can explicitly append clean-state diagnostics when AppendClean is set.
    The helper can disable history append entirely when DisableHistoryAppend is set.
    The helper returns structured classification/history result data.

Still true:

    No deletes.
    No restores.
    No reset execution.
    No trust.json mutation.
    No identity-candidates.json mutation.
    No verification.
    No key replacement.
    No send/open/ack behavior change.
    No CLI/registry exposure.
    No local-backbone.
    No device_verified/device_key_changed/device_revoked emission from recovery orchestration.

### 0.5 v0.5.29 Implementation Details

New input type:

    IdentityRecoveryOrchestrationInput

Fields:

    RecoveryInput
    DisableHistoryAppend
    AppendClean

New result type:

    IdentityRecoveryOrchestrationResult

Fields:

    Classification
    HistoryEvent
    HistoryAppended
    HistorySkippedReason

New helper:

    OrchestrateIdentityRecovery(input)

Behavior:

    calls ClassifyIdentityRecovery(input.RecoveryInput);
    returns classification even when no history is appended;
    if DisableHistoryAppend is true, skips append and records "history append disabled";
    if classification is recovery_clean_local_state and AppendClean is false, skips append and records "clean recovery classification not appended by default";
    otherwise builds a recovery-history draft through BuildIdentityRecoveryHistoryDraft;
    appends through AppendIdentityRecoveryHistoryEvent;
    returns the appended event pointer and HistoryAppended=true.

New policy helper:

    ShouldAppendIdentityRecoveryHistoryByDefault(classification)

Default append policy:

    append by default when classification string is non-empty and not recovery_clean_local_state;
    do not append recovery_clean_local_state by default.

Explicit diagnostic behavior:

    recovery_clean_local_state can still append when AppendClean=true.

### 0.6 v0.5.29 Tests Added

Tests cover:

    clean local state skips history by default;
    clean local state can be explicitly appended with AppendClean;
    missing trust store classification appends recovery history;
    missing trust history classification appends recovery history and creates the event log if needed;
    missing candidate store classification appends recovery history without creating identity-candidates.json;
    corrupt trust store classification appends recovery history without mutating corrupt trust.json;
    corrupt trust history classification appends recovery history without repairing/replacing the corrupt prefix;
    corrupt candidate store classification appends recovery history without mutating identity-candidates.json;
    DisableHistoryAppend returns classification but does not append;
    orchestration does not emit device_verified/device_key_changed/device_revoked;
    ShouldAppendIdentityRecoveryHistoryByDefault skips clean/empty and appends missing-trust-store.

### 0.5 v0.5.28 Implementation Details

New draft type:

    IdentityRecoveryHistoryDraft

Fields:

    AccountID

    PreviousTrustState

    Note
    NowUTC

New helpers:

    BuildIdentityRecoveryHistoryDraft(classification IdentityRecoveryClassification)
      Converts a recovery classification into an append-only recovery-history draft.
      Source defaults to identity_recovery_classifier.
      NewTrustState stores the recovery classification string.
      Note stores classification metadata and safety flags.

    BuildIdentityRecoveryHistoryEvent(draft IdentityRecoveryHistoryDraft)
      Converts a recovery-history draft into a trust.Event-compatible shape without writing it.

    AppendIdentityRecoveryHistoryEvent(paths Paths, draft IdentityRecoveryHistoryDraft)
      Appends a recovery-history event to trust-events.jsonl through AppendProviderEvent.

Internal mapping:

    identityRecoveryEventType(classification)
      Allows the current RecoveryClassification* strings as event names.

    identityRecoveryHistoryProviderDraft(draft)
      Converts the recovery-history draft into ProviderEventAppendDraft and rejects device trust mutation event names.

    identityRecoveryHistoryNote(classification)
      Preserves classification, severity, state-file presence booleans, review/reverify/reenrollment/block flags, explicit non-mutation/non-verification flags, and normalized reason text.

## 0. v0.5.26 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.26 is an implementation rung following the v0.5.25 reset/recovery/re-enrollment boundary decision.

v0.5.25 decided that reset/recovery/re-enrollment semantics must be classified before destructive reset/recovery/re-enrollment helpers, before CLI/registry exposure, and before local-backbone work.

v0.5.26 implements the first narrow classification layer:

    carbonstack-comms/internal/trust/identity_recovery.go
    carbonstack-comms/internal/trust/identity_recovery_test.go

Meaning:

    Comms can now classify local trust/candidate/history recovery conditions without mutating state.
    Missing/corrupt trust store, trust history, and candidate store states are distinguished.
    Known revoked/compromised/changed devices are treated as recovery blockers or reverify cases.
    Candidate conflict/rejected/unverified states are mapped to review/reverify/re-enrollment outcomes.
    Mismatch classifier outputs can be folded into recovery classifications.

Still true:

    The helper does not delete files.
    The helper does not restore files.
    The helper does not execute reset.
    The helper does not mutate trust.json.
    The helper does not append trust-events.jsonl.
    The helper does not mutate identity-candidates.json.
    The helper does not verify identity.
    The helper does not replace key material.
    The helper does not affect send/open/ack behavior.
    The helper does not expose CLI/registry behavior.
    The helper does not create local-backbone.

    recovery_requires_reenrollment
    recovery_blocked_revoked
    recovery_blocked_compromised

New input type:

    IdentityRecoveryInput

Input fields:

    Paths
    CandidatesPath
    Candidate
    KnownDevice
    MismatchDecision

New result type:

    IdentityRecoveryClassification

Result fields include:

    Classification
    Severity
    TrustStorePresent
    TrustHistoryPresent
    CandidateStorePresent
    RequiresReview
    RequiresReverify
    RequiresReenrollment
    BlocksSend
    BlocksPromotion
    MayMutateTrustStore
    MayAppendTrustHistory
    MayMutateCandidateStore
    MayVerifyIdentity
    MayReplaceKeyMaterial
    Reason

New error:

    ErrIdentityRecoveryInputInvalid

New main helper:

    ClassifyIdentityRecovery(input)

Classification order:

    validate required paths;
    classify trust.json presence/corruption;
    classify trust-events.jsonl presence/corruption;
    classify identity-candidates.json presence/corruption;
    classify known revoked/compromised/changed device blockers;
    classify mismatch decisions requiring reverify/conflict/block;
    classify candidate conflict/rejected/unverified state;
    otherwise classify clean local state.

File inspection behavior:

    trust.json is read and JSON-decoded into Store.
    trust-events.jsonl is checked with LoadEvents.
    identity-candidates.json is read and JSON-decoded into IdentityCandidateStore.

Mutation behavior:

    No writes.
    No appends.
    No deletes.
    No restore behavior.

### 0.8 Significance

v0.5.26 turns the v0.5.25 reset/recovery/re-enrollment boundary from documentation into a first test-backed internal classifier.

This matters because the candidate identity pipeline is now strong enough to observe, store, classify, review, append history, and orchestrate candidate observations, but local-backbone still needs safe recovery semantics before it can make honest claims.

v0.5.26 reduces the reset/recovery blocker by proving that Comms can inspect trust/candidate/history files and recovery inputs without changing state.

It still does not justify local-backbone, CLI/registry exposure, destructive reset helpers, recovery helpers, verified identity import, mature UX, or production trust claims.

### 0.5 v0.5.25 Decision Details

Definitions:

    Reset:
      deliberate discard or reinitialization of local state.
      Not verification, recovery, trust continuity, key replacement, or re-enrollment.

    Recovery:
      restoring or reusing prior local state after loss, corruption, migration, or reinstall.
      Recovery does not automatically prove trust continuity and must fail loudly on conflicts.

    Re-enrollment:
      deliberately introducing new local identity/device material after loss, rotation, compromise, reinstall, or migration.
      Re-enrollment is not verification and should first produce candidate/unverified state unless a mature verification ceremony exists.

State domains that must be distinguished:

    local app state;
    trust.json;
    trust-events.jsonl;
    identity-candidates.json;
    OpenMLS provider state;
    relay staging artifacts;
    generated dev artifacts;
    Cypher server state as downstream context.

Core rules:

    trust.json is trust-bearing state.
    trust-events.jsonl is trust-history state.
    identity-candidates.json is trust-adjacent candidate state.
    OpenMLS provider state is identity/group/conversation-bearing state.
    Relay staging artifacts can be safe to reset in dev flows, but must not weaken ack/open policy.
    Cypher reset/recovery remains downstream and must not become identity authority.

### 0.6 Recovery Classification Direction

v0.5.25 proposes future recovery classifications such as:

    recovery_clean_local_state
    recovery_missing_trust_store
    recovery_missing_trust_history
    recovery_missing_candidate_store
    recovery_missing_provider_state
    recovery_corrupt_trust_store
    recovery_corrupt_trust_history
    recovery_corrupt_candidate_store
    recovery_corrupt_provider_state
    recovery_provider_identity_mismatch
    recovery_candidate_conflict
    recovery_requires_reverify
    recovery_requires_reenrollment
    recovery_blocked_revoked
    recovery_blocked_compromised

Future classification helpers should be pure/non-mutating first.

### 0.7 Reset Scope Direction

v0.5.25 proposes explicit reset scopes:

    generated_dev_artifacts
    relay_staging
    candidate_state
    trust_history
    trust_store
    provider_state
    local_app_state
    all_comms_local_state

Dangerous scopes:

    trust_store
    trust_history
    provider_state
    all_comms_local_state

Dangerous scopes should never hide behind a generic reset command.

### 0.8 Re-enrollment Boundary

Re-enrollment should be deliberate.

It should:

    create or observe candidate identity material;
    preserve old known trust state;
    append history later where appropriate;
    require review/reverify;
    avoid silent replacement;
    avoid verified import.

It must not:

    call VerifyDevice automatically;
    call MarkDeviceChanged automatically from provider observation alone;
    replace PublicIdentityKey automatically;
    mark verified automatically;
    bypass candidate review;
    ack messages;
    weaken send/open policy.

### 0.9 Trust-History / Send-Open-Ack Boundaries

Reset/recovery/re-enrollment may append history later, but history append must remain separate from trust mutation.

Do not emit:

    device_verified
    device_key_changed
    device_revoked

unless an explicit mature ceremony/mutation/revocation flow is actually being executed.

Send/open/ack rules remain:

    missing or reset trust does not imply safe send;
    recovered provider state does not imply verified trust;
    re-enrolled device material does not imply verified trust;
    message retrieval does not imply message-open success;
    artifact write does not imply ack;
    history append does not imply ack.

## 0. v0.5.24 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.24 is an implementation rung following the v0.5.23 candidate/mismatch trust-history append helpers.

v0.5.23 established append-only trust-history event helper surfaces for candidate observations, candidate review/update results, and mapped mismatch classifier decisions.

v0.5.24 adds the first narrow internal orchestration layer:

    carbonstack-comms/internal/trust/identity_candidate_orchestration.go
    carbonstack-comms/internal/trust/identity_candidate_orchestration_test.go

Meaning:

    A candidate observation can now be processed through a single internal trust helper.
    The helper adds/dedupes the candidate in identity-candidates.json.
    The helper optionally looks up a known local device by claimed_device_id only.
    The helper classifies the candidate using the existing pure mismatch classifier.
    The helper appends one selected trust-history event only when the candidate is newly added.
    Duplicate observations are deduped and do not append duplicate history.
    The helper returns a structured result containing the stored candidate, whether it was added, whether a known device was found, the classifier decision, and an optional appended history event.

Still true:

    The helper does not mutate trust.json.
    The helper does not verify identity.
    The helper does not replace key material.
    The helper does not emit device_verified, device_key_changed, or device_revoked.
    The helper does not affect send/open/ack behavior.
    The helper does not expose CLI/registry behavior.
    The helper does not create local-backbone.
    The helper does not wire broad live provider import.

### 0.5 v0.5.24 Implementation Details

New error:

    ErrIdentityCandidateObservationInvalid

New result type:

    IdentityCandidateObservationResult

Result fields:

    Candidate
    CandidateAdded
    KnownDeviceFound
    Decision
    HistoryEvent
    HistoryAppended

New helper:

    ObserveIdentityCandidate(paths, candidatesPath, candidate)

Input validation:

    candidatesPath must not be empty.
    paths.TrustPath must not be empty.
    paths.EventsPath must not be empty.
    candidate must pass AddIdentityCandidate / NormalizeIdentityCandidate validation.

Flow:

    AddIdentityCandidate(candidatesPath, candidate)
      Adds candidate to identity-candidates.json if new.
      Returns existing candidate if deduped.

    LookupDevice(paths, storedCandidate.ClaimedDeviceID)
      Runs only when claimed_device_id is non-empty.
      Does not invent mappings.
      Does not import provider identity.
      Does not verify candidate identity.

    ClassifyIdentityMismatch(...)
      Runs using stored candidate and optional known device.
      Remains pure/non-mutating.

    If candidate was not newly added:
      Return result.
      Do not append history.

    If candidate was newly added and no known device was found:
      BuildIdentityCandidateObservedHistoryDraft.
      AppendIdentityCandidateHistoryEvent.

    If candidate was newly added and known device was found:
      BuildIdentityMismatchHistoryDraft.
      AppendIdentityCandidateHistoryEvent.

Append behavior:

    Writes trust-events.jsonl only through the existing append path.
    Does not write trust.json.
    Does not write identity-candidates.json beyond the earlier AddIdentityCandidate step.
    Does not emit device_verified/device_key_changed/device_revoked.

### 0.6 v0.5.24 Tests Added

Tests cover:

    ObserveIdentityCandidate adds a new candidate and appends provider_identity_candidate_observed.
    Unmapped observation creates identity-candidates.json and trust-events.jsonl, but not trust.json.
    Duplicate observation dedupes candidate and does not append duplicate history.
    Known verified matching device appends provider_identity_continuity_observed.
    Known verified matching device does not mutate existing verified trust state or fingerprint.
    Known verified mismatching device appends provider_identity_reverify_required.
    Known verified mismatch does not replace existing key/fingerprint and leaves trust state verified.
    Known revoked device appends provider_identity_promotion_blocked_revoked.
    Known revoked device remains revoked.
    Invalid inputs are rejected:
        empty candidate path;
        empty trust path;
        invalid candidate missing fingerprint.
    Observation path does not emit device_verified, device_key_changed, or device_revoked.

v0.5.24 does not:

### 0.8 Significance

v0.5.24 is the first rung where candidate observation, storage, classification, and append-only history are connected in one internal helper.

This is significant because earlier rungs created isolated pieces:

    v0.5.19: candidate identity storage.
    v0.5.20: pure mapped identity mismatch classifier.

v0.5.24 composes those pieces in a narrow non-user-facing path without expanding claims.

It moves CarbonStack closer to a future local-backbone validation story, but it still does not justify local-backbone, CLI/registry exposure, verified identity import, mature UX, or production trust claims.

### 0.5 v0.5.23 Implementation Details

New event-name constants:

    IdentityCandidateEventObserved           = "provider_identity_candidate_observed"
    IdentityCandidateEventReviewStarted      = "provider_identity_candidate_review_started"
    IdentityCandidateEventRejected           = "provider_identity_candidate_rejected"
    IdentityCandidateEventMarkedUnverified   = "provider_identity_candidate_marked_unverified"
    IdentityCandidateEventConflict           = "provider_identity_candidate_conflict"
    IdentityCandidateEventReverifyRequired   = "provider_identity_reverify_required"
    IdentityCandidateEventContinuityObserved = "provider_identity_continuity_observed"
    IdentityCandidateEventBlockedRevoked     = "provider_identity_promotion_blocked_revoked"
    IdentityCandidateEventBlockedCompromised = "provider_identity_promotion_blocked_compromised"
    IdentityCandidateEventChangedCandidate   = "provider_identity_changed_candidate"

New type:

    IdentityCandidateHistoryDraft

New error:

    ErrIdentityCandidateHistoryDraftInvalid

New helper surfaces:

    BuildIdentityCandidateObservedHistoryDraft
    BuildIdentityCandidateReviewHistoryDraft
    BuildIdentityMismatchHistoryDraft
    BuildIdentityCandidateHistoryEvent
    AppendIdentityCandidateHistoryEvent
    identityCandidateHistoryProviderDraft
    identityCandidateReviewEventType
    identityMismatchEventType
    identityCandidateHistoryNote

Observed candidate behavior:

    Normalizes IdentityCandidate.
    Creates provider_identity_candidate_observed history draft.
    Carries account_id, claimed_device_id, fingerprint, observed_at, candidate state, and provenance into a trust-history-compatible draft.
    Does not write anything.

Review/update behavior:

    Converts IdentityCandidateReviewResult into event types:
        pending_review -> provider_identity_candidate_review_started
        rejected -> provider_identity_candidate_rejected
        unverified -> provider_identity_candidate_marked_unverified
        conflicts_known_device -> provider_identity_candidate_conflict
    Rejects unsupported candidate states such as observed for review-history draft purposes.
    Does not perform candidate-store update itself; caller must update candidate state separately.

Mismatch behavior:

    Converts IdentityMismatchDecision classifications into event types:
        candidate_only -> provider_identity_candidate_observed
        continuity_observation -> provider_identity_continuity_observed
        review_required_conflict -> provider_identity_candidate_conflict
        reverify_required -> provider_identity_reverify_required
        changed_candidate -> provider_identity_changed_candidate
        blocked_revoked -> provider_identity_promotion_blocked_revoked
        blocked_compromised -> provider_identity_promotion_blocked_compromised

Append behavior:

    AppendIdentityCandidateHistoryEvent converts IdentityCandidateHistoryDraft into ProviderEventAppendDraft, then uses AppendProviderEvent.
    AppendProviderEvent ultimately writes only trust-events.jsonl through AppendEvent.
    The append path does not mutate trust.json.
    The append path does not write identity-candidates.json.

Safety guard:

    identityCandidateHistoryProviderDraft rejects these event types:
        device_verified
        device_key_changed
        device_revoked

This protects the candidate/mismatch append integration from pretending to perform mature trust-store mutation events.

### 0.6 v0.5.23 Tests Added

Tests cover:

    BuildIdentityCandidateObservedHistoryDraft.
    Observed candidate note contains context, candidate id, candidate state, source, source detail, provider event.
    BuildIdentityCandidateReviewHistoryDraft.
    Review result for rejected candidate becomes provider_identity_candidate_rejected.
    Unsupported review history state is rejected.
    BuildIdentityMismatchHistoryDraft for reverify_required.
    Mismatch note contains classification, known trust state, review/reverify/send-block flags.
    Mapping coverage for all current mismatch classifier classifications.
    BuildIdentityCandidateHistoryEvent rejects device_verified, device_key_changed, and device_revoked.
    AppendIdentityCandidateHistoryEvent writes trust-events.jsonl only.
    AppendIdentityCandidateHistoryEvent does not mutate trust.json.
    AppendIdentityCandidateHistoryEvent does not write identity-candidates.json.

Update behavior:

    Locate candidate by candidate_id when provided.
    Otherwise locate candidate by deterministic dedupe key through a normalized DedupeCandidate.
    Validate requested new state against candidate-state allowlist.

    Save only identity-candidates.json through SaveIdentityCandidateStore.
    Preserve candidate raw identity material, fingerprint, source, and provenance fields.
    Append simple reviewer/updated_at/review note text into the existing note field when provided.

Current transition policy:

    observed -> pending_review
    observed -> rejected
    observed -> unverified
    observed -> conflicts_known_device

    pending_review -> rejected
    pending_review -> unverified
    pending_review -> conflicts_known_device

    conflicts_known_device -> pending_review
    conflicts_known_device -> rejected

    unverified -> rejected

Rejected is sticky for the first implementation.

No transition to verified is allowed.

### 0.5 v0.5.20 Implementation Details

New classification constants:

    IdentityMismatchClassificationCandidateOnly          = "candidate_only"
    IdentityMismatchClassificationContinuity             = "continuity_observation"
    IdentityMismatchClassificationReviewRequiredConflict = "review_required_conflict"
    IdentityMismatchClassificationReverifyRequired       = "reverify_required"
    IdentityMismatchClassificationChangedCandidate       = "changed_candidate"
    IdentityMismatchClassificationBlockedRevoked         = "blocked_revoked"
    IdentityMismatchClassificationBlockedCompromised     = "blocked_compromised"

New input/output types:

    IdentityMismatchInput
    IdentityMismatchDecision

Input fields:

    Candidate
    KnownDevice
    MappingPresent

Decision fields:

    classification
    known_trust_state
    candidate_state
    has_known_device
    material_matches
    requires_review
    requires_reverify
    blocks_send
    blocks_promotion
    may_append_history
    may_mutate_trust_store
    may_verify_identity
    may_replace_key_material
    reason

New helper/error surfaces:

    ErrIdentityMismatchInputInvalid
    ClassifyIdentityMismatch
    identityCandidateMatchesKnownDevice

Important current behavior:

    ClassifyIdentityMismatch normalizes candidate input through NormalizeIdentityCandidate.
    Missing mapping or nil known device classifies as candidate_only and blocks strict mature send.
    Verified known device + matching material classifies as continuity_observation and does not block send by itself.
    Verified known device + different material classifies as reverify_required, requires review, requires reverify, and blocks send.
    Unverified/unknown known device + matching material classifies as continuity_observation but still blocks strict mature send.
    Unverified/unknown known device + different material classifies as review_required_conflict and blocks send.
    Changed known device classifies as changed_candidate, requires review/reverify, and blocks send.
    Revoked known device classifies as blocked_revoked and blocks promotion/send.
    Compromised-reserved known device classifies as blocked_compromised and blocks promotion/send.
    Material comparison prefers fingerprint match when both fingerprints are present and equal.
    Material comparison falls back to raw public identity material equality when usable.

Hardcoded safety decisions:

    MayMutateTrustStore is false.
    MayVerifyIdentity is false.
    MayReplaceKeyMaterial is false.

### 0.6 v0.5.20 Tests Added

Tests cover:

    Candidate-only classification when no mapping exists.
    Verified known device with matching material -> continuity observation.
    Verified known device with different material -> reverify required.
    Unverified known device with matching material -> continuity but strict-send block remains.
    Unverified known device with different material -> review-required conflict.
    Changed known device -> changed-candidate and reverify required.
    Revoked known device -> promotion/send blocked.
    Compromised-reserved known device -> promotion/send blocked.
    Invalid candidate input is rejected.
    Raw public identity material fallback can produce a match.
    Pure classifier does not authorize trust mutation, verification, or key replacement.

    SaveIdentityCandidateStore
    AddIdentityCandidate
    NormalizeIdentityCandidate
    IsAllowedIdentityCandidateState
    IdentityCandidateDedupeKey
    IdentityCandidateID

Storage behavior:

    Load missing identity-candidates.json as an empty store.
    Save JSON object with identity_candidates array.
    Create parent directory with 0700 permissions when needed.
    Write store file with 0600 permissions.
    Normalize candidate fields before adding.
    Default blank candidate_state to observed.
    Default blank observed_at to NowUTC().
    Default blank candidate_id to deterministic IdentityCandidateID().
    Require fingerprint.
    Require source.
    Reject any candidate_state outside the allowlist.
    Reject StateVerified as an invalid candidate state.

Dedupe behavior:

    Primary dedupe key:
        claimed_device_id + fingerprint + source

    If claimed_device_id is blank:
        fingerprint + source

Candidate ID behavior:

    candidate_id defaults to:
        candidate- + first 8 bytes of sha256(dedupe key) as hex

## 0. v0.5.18 Current Overlay

### 0.1 Summary

v0.5.18 is a docs/decision-only breakpoint.

Decision:

### 0.5 v0.5.18 Decision Details

Candidate identity storage owner:

    carbonstack-comms/internal/trust

Reason:

    Candidate identity material is local trust-adjacent state.
    It is not provider protocol truth.
    It will later interact with trust state, review status, mismatch classification, verification ceremony, and future vault boundaries.

Preferred storage file:

    .carbonstack-comms/identity-candidates.json

Preferred first file shape:

    JSON object containing an identity_candidates array.

Initial candidate states:

    observed
    pending_review
    unverified
    conflicts_known_device
    rejected

Deferred states:

    stale
    promoted_to_unverified
    promoted_to_verified_by_ceremony

Raw identity material policy:

    Allowed only as dev/pre-alpha local state for comparison.
    Must be clearly documented as sensitive-ish and future-vault-bound.
    Candidate records should store a fingerprint too.

Dedupe policy:

    Primary:
        claimed_device_id + fingerprint + source

    If claimed_device_id is blank:
        fingerprint + source

Verify stub decision:

    Do not add a verify stub yet.
    Verification wording is dangerous before ceremony/storage/vault behavior is designed.
    Registry entries should wait until an actual command/profile/script/API surface exists.

Research fallback:

    If implementation becomes too tangled, use an unstable/non-production research folder or revisit the storage model.

Possible fallback path:

    carbonstack-comms/internal/trust/research/*

Rules for fallback research folder:

    unstable;
    non-prod;
    not release-facing;
    used only to learn an implementation shape;
    lessons must be brought back into mainline deliberately.

## 1. Current Project Goal

**Active goal:** Continue v0.5.x after the provider/trust/candidate/mismatch and Relay Space planning arc by using the v0.5.17 roadmap refresh as the current public planning baseline. v0.5.17 concluded that local-backbone is closer and architecture-discussable, but not implementation-ready. The next work should choose a narrow implementation-priority target instead of creating local-backbone or overclaiming deployment readiness.

Current working priority order:

    1. state correctness and persistence;
    2. concrete state-domain inventory;
    3. storage-domain model;
    4. trust-state model;
    5. provider-state linkage plan;
    6. provider-trust decision report helper;
    7. provider-trust report contract / JSON-vs-summary semantics;
    8. provider-trust report exposure decision;
    9. provider-originated trust history planning before any mutation;
    10. provider-originated trust event naming / append-only rules;
    11. provider trust-history draft helper for selected security-relevant events;
    12. provider trust-event draft bridge to a trust.Event-compatible shape;
    13. provider trust-event append helper owned by internal/trust;
    14. provider identity candidate/unverified import plan;
    15. mapped provider identity mismatch -> changed/reverify plan;
    16. Relay Space architecture recon and decision record after provider-linkage/history is coherent;
    17. local-backbone feasibility reassessment and roadmap refresh decision;
    18. roadmap-refresh aftermath / implementation-priority decision;
    18. candidate/storage implementation planning after Relay Space/local-backbone readiness is re-evaluated;
    19. vault boundary design after domains are understood;
    20. PQ/hybrid migration recon after state/trust/provider boundaries are clear.

CarbonStack’s broader intent remains:

- **CarbonStack** is the secure-communications appliance-stack project and shared doctrine/release authority.
- **CarbonStackComms** is the text-first messaging client and current OpenMLS sidecar/relay integration surface.
- **CarbonStackCypher** is the self-hostable relay/storage stack.
- **CarbonStackOS** is future constrained Android-derived appliance OS work and remains out of current runnable validation packages.
- The `carbonstack` Gitea repo remains the source of truth for release state, release assets, docs, registry, and public claims.
- GitHub mirrors are secondary push mirrors for discoverability/redundancy only.
- Raw CarbonStack LogDoc and breakpoint files are private handoff artifacts unless deliberately sanitized and promoted.

**North star:**

> Its goal is not to be a better smartphone. Its goal is to stop being a smartphone.

**Core doctrine:**

> Every feature is guilty until it proves it does not add unacceptable parser, network, sensor, identity, or filesystem authority.

### 4.5 v0.5.6 provider-state linkage plan

v0.5.6 planned how OpenMLS sidecar/provider events should eventually link into Comms trust history, warnings, blocking behavior, recovery expectations, and implementation staging.

Key v0.5.6 decisions:

    Comms device ID remains the local trust record key until a mature identity key is designed.
    Sidecar labels are dev/operator handles, not mature identity truth.
    Provider public identity material is the future bridge, but current production-grade safety-number material is not finalized.
    Observed provider public identity material should create unknown/unverified candidate state unless verified by ceremony.
    Matching provider material can support continuity checks for already verified devices.
    Mismatching provider material must become changed / reverify-required behavior.
    KeyPackages are setup artifacts, not automatically verified identity.
    Provider events should feed trust history only after explicit policy mapping.
    Unknown future provider events should not automatically become fatal or trust-mutating.
    Trust-security and terminal-fatal events must be loud and conservative.

### 4.12 v0.5.13 provider trust-event append helper

v0.5.13 crossed the write boundary for the first time, but only in the narrowest trust-owned way.

Implementation added in `carbonstack-comms`:

    internal/trust/provider_events.go
    internal/trust/provider_events_test.go

New trust-package input shape:

    ProviderEventAppendDraft

New error/helper surfaces:

    ErrProviderEventAppendDraftInvalid
    BuildProviderEvent
    AppendProviderEvent

Behavior:

    BuildProviderEvent converts a ProviderEventAppendDraft into a trust.Event without writing it to disk.
    AppendProviderEvent converts the draft and writes only to `trust-events.jsonl` via AppendEvent.
    Source defaults to `provider_event_append` if blank.
    EventTime defaults to `trust.NowUTC()` if blank.
    EventID is generated using the existing trust.EventID() helper.
    Missing account/device/fingerprint mapping is allowed and preserved as empty.
    The helper only writes the event log and does not mutate the trust store.

Final v0.5.13 commit:

    carbonstack-comms:
      e7e8cc5 feat: add provider trust event append helper

Important boundary:

v0.5.14 returned to planning-only after v0.5.13 crossed the narrow trust-history append boundary.

Core plan:

    Provider-observed identity material is not trust.
    It may become a candidate, unverified record, append-only history event, warning, reverify-required condition, or block condition.

    It must not silently replace a known device.
    It must not make Cypher delivery an identity authority.
    It must not make sidecar labels an identity authority.

Storage options considered:

    Option B: identity-candidates.json.
    Option C: append-only history first.
    Option D: future vault-bound pending identity domain.

### 4.14 v0.5.15 mapped provider identity mismatch -> changed/reverify plan

v0.5.15 completed the mapped provider identity mismatch planning rung.

Public docs added:

    carbonstack/docs/177-v0.5.15-mapped-provider-identity-mismatch-plan-v0.md
    carbonstack-comms/docs/12-mapped-provider-identity-mismatch-plan-v0.md

Public docs updated:

    carbonstack/docs/README.md
    carbonstack-comms/README.md

Core plan:

    Provider identity mismatch is a security-relevant observation.
    It is not automatically a verified fact.
    It must not automatically verify a device, replace a known device key, mutate trust.json, un-revoke a device, trust Cypher as identity authority, or trust sidecar labels as identity authority.

Mapped/unmapped definitions:

    Mapped provider identity = provider-observed identity material that can be associated with a local Comms device record through some evidence.
    Mapping evidence does not equal verification.
    Unmapped provider identity = no safe association with a local Comms device record; may become candidate only, but must not mutate existing trusted records.
    Identity mismatch = observed provider identity material differs from expected material for a mapped local device.

Case matrix recorded:

    no known mapping -> candidate-only / history-only; no trust.json mutation; no changed state;
    known unverified device, same material -> continuity observation; remain unverified;
    known unverified device, different material -> review-required conflict; strict send blocks;
    known verified device, same material -> continuity observation; verified state remains unchanged;
    known verified device, different material -> reverify-required; strict send blocks; later implementation may mark changed only with explicit mapped-mutation policy;
    known changed device -> preserve changed; require reverify;
    known revoked device -> block promotion; do not un-revoke;
    known compromised-reserved device -> block promotion; keep behavior reserved.

Future event names proposed:

    provider_identity_candidate_observed
    provider_identity_candidate_conflict
    provider_identity_continuity_observed
    provider_identity_mismatch_detected
    provider_identity_reverify_required
    provider_identity_changed_mapped
    provider_identity_promotion_blocked_revoked
    provider_identity_promotion_blocked_compromised

Trust-event boundary:

    device_verified remains reserved for explicit verification ceremony.
    device_key_changed remains reserved for actual trust-state mutation to changed.
    device_revoked remains reserved for explicit revocation flow.

Future mutation gate:

    A later implementation may mutate trust.json only when mapping exists, mismatch policy classifies the case as changed/reverify-required, tests prove no verified identity is created from provider observation, strict send blocks changed/reverify states, history is appended before or alongside mutation, and user-visible warning/recovery behavior is defined.

Validation:

    Failure-tracking wrapper was used.
    v0.5.15 comms go test ./... passed.
    v0.5.15 runner go test ./... passed.
    v0.5.15 runner doctor passed.
    Overall wrapper printed `VALIDATION PASSED`.

## 8. Critical Blunders / Lessons to Carry Forward

### 8.1 LogDoc continuity ledger semantics

User clarified during v0.5.8 that Markdown LogDocs are intended as continuity ledgers.

Rule:

    Keep previous breakpoint context.
    Append current breakpoint timeline information.
    Do not reduce the Markdown into only a terse current-state summary.
    Do not imitate PRIME length for ordinary rungs.
    Use PRIME style only at minor-epoch / pre-compression handoffs.

### 8.2 Raw handoff files are private

Raw CarbonStackLogDocV*.md and CarbonStack_BreakpointV*.json files are for user + assistant continuity.

They should not be committed to the public repo.

Public repo LogDoc material should be sanitized PRIME/minor-epoch material only, placed manually under sanitized-project-logdoc-list.

### 8.3 JSON source-of-truth rule for provider-trust reports

ProviderTrustReport structured fields are the diagnostic source of truth.

Human summaries are interpretive helper text.

Future commands/docs must not let summary strings become policy or test source of truth.

### 8.4 No command means no registry update

v0.5.15 still did not add a CLI command, runner profile, script, API surface, or sidecar command.

Therefore no registry update was required.

If a future provider-trust-report-dev command is added, update registry/commands.v0.yaml and registry tests in the same or next checkpoint.

### 8.5 Commit metadata warning remains unresolved

Commits still show local committer metadata:

    bitcrusher32 <Bitcrusher32@▓▓.localdomain>

Not a v0.5.15 blocker.

Eventually configure Git author/committer metadata cleanly for professionalism/publishing hygiene.

### 8.6 Ack policy remains sacred

No future provider-report, trust-history, event-draft, append-helper, candidate-identity, mismatch, or Relay Space implementation should ack a message before successful sidecar open/consume.

The old v0.4.x lesson still applies:

    retrieval is not enough;
    artifact write is not enough;
    report generation is not enough;
    trust-history append is not enough;
    history draft generation is not enough;
    event draft generation is not enough;
    candidate import is not enough;
    mismatch classification is not enough;
    sidecar message-open success is required;
    only then may ack happen.

### 8.7 Append is not mutation

A provider-originated trust-history append does not automatically imply trust.json mutation.

Append can record safety history.

Mutation changes device trust state.

These must remain separate unless a later checkpoint explicitly couples them for mapped device identity cases.

### 8.8 Protocol remains policy/draft-only

v0.5.13 deliberately keeps `internal/protocol` out of `internal/trust`.

Pattern:

    internal/protocol:
      provider event taxonomy;
      trust decisions;
      reports;
      history drafts;
      trust.Event-compatible drafts.

    internal/trust:
      trust.Event;
      trust-events.jsonl append behavior;
      trust.json load/save/mutation behavior.

This avoids coupling provider policy to storage writes too early.

### 8.9 Validation wrappers should summarize global status

Use a failure-tracking wrapper or `set -e`.

Prefer failure-tracking wrappers when we want all failures summarized.

A single profile's `VALIDATION PASSED` is not proof that the whole multi-command validation block passed.

v0.5.15 used the failure-tracking wrapper and passed all steps.

Minor note:

    The pasted v0.5.15 validation block still displayed shell-tail glue around the final else block, but the all-pass path executed and the wrapper printed overall VALIDATION PASSED. Prefer cleaner smaller copy blocks if tail glue becomes harmful.

### 8.10 Test action-order brittleness

Do not make tests brittle around action slice order in interpretive note strings unless order itself is policy.

For provider-trust history draft notes, test presence of required flags/tokens rather than exact joined action order.

### 8.11 Push authentication can fail once

v0.5.13 first `git push` failed authentication once.

Second `git push` succeeded.

Not a project blocker, but keep in mind during validation/commit logs:

    authenticate retry success is acceptable;
    final snapshot must still show origin/main aligned.

### 8.12 Research-folder fallback remains available, not default

User suggested a possible fallback workflow if provider/trust or PQ implementation becomes too dicey:

    carbonstack-comms/internal/protocol/trust/research/*

or similar unstable/non-prod research folder.

Consensus:

    Use normal internal/protocol/internal/trust first when the work is clean and narrow.
    Use research folder only if implementation becomes conceptually risky or too tangled.
    Same model may be useful later for PQ readiness/testing if it becomes technically dicey.

### 8.13 Roadmap refresh timing

Do not refresh the long-term roadmap after every rung.

Likely refresh window remains around v0.5.17, with possible slip to v0.5.18 if Relay Space planning expands.

Refresh after the current planning arc is complete enough:

    provider-trust report exposure decision complete;
    provider event -> trust history append plan/implementation complete enough;
    provider identity candidate/import/mismatch plan complete;
    Relay Space architecture decision record complete;
    local-backbone feasibility reassessment complete;
    PQ/vault ordering re-evaluated.

    [VALIDATION WRAPPER PATTERN]
    cd ~/repos/carbonstack_umbrella
    failures=()
    run_step() {
      name="$1"
      shift
      echo
      echo "===== $name ====="
      if "$@"; then
        echo "PASS: $name"
      else
        rc=$?
        echo "FAIL: $name rc=$rc"
        failures+=("$name rc=$rc")
      fi
    }
    # run_step "name" command args...

## 10. v0.5.x Forward Plan

### Immediate next: v0.5.18 roadmap-refresh aftermath / implementation-priority decision

Goal:

    Decide which narrow post-planning implementation or planning spike should happen first after the v0.5.17 roadmap refresh.

Default recommendation:

    Do not create local-backbone next.
    Do not create a public deployment claim.
    Choose one targeted spike that reduces ambiguity without overclaiming.

Candidate v0.5.18 directions:

    candidate identity draft/storage spike;
    mapped mismatch classifier spike;
    provider-event live-flow append integration spike;
    Relay Space join/invite/member planning;
    validation profile boundary planning;
    reset/recovery/re-enrollment planning.

Suggested decision criteria:

    Does the rung reduce a blocker identified by v0.5.17?
    Does it preserve provider observation != trust?
    Does it preserve append != mutation?
    Does it preserve ack-after-open?
    Does it avoid making Relay Space or Cypher identity authority?
    Does it avoid claiming local-backbone readiness too early?

### After v0.5.18

Likely next sequence depends on the chosen priority:

    If candidate identity is chosen:
      define and test candidate draft/storage without verified promotion.

    If mapped mismatch is chosen:
      implement classifier only, with tests proving no provider observation creates verified trust.

    If provider-event live-flow append is chosen:
      wire only a tiny safe allowlist, with no trust.json mutation and no ack changes.

    If Relay Space planning is chosen:
      define join/invite/member lifecycle before schema/API work.

    If validation profile boundary is chosen:
      define what a future local-backbone profile would prove and not prove before implementation.

### Roadmap refresh status

The v0.5.17 roadmap refresh is complete.

Do not refresh the long-term roadmap again after every rung.

Refresh again only when:

    implementation priorities materially change;
    v0.5.x is approaching v0.6.0;
    a public release package is being planned;
    a major claim boundary changes.

v0.5.17 is stable and safe to pause.

Current heads:

    carbonstack-comms  94e0ff2 docs: record Comms Relay Space boundary
    carbonstack-cypher 24166b0 docs: record Relay Space boundary
    carbonstack-os     1bbbe52 docs: clarify CarbonStackOS target direction

Current truth:

    The current public release remains v0.5.0.
    v0.5.17 is a mainline post-release planning/checkpoint rung, not a public release.
    carbonstack/docs now include the v0.5.17 local-backbone feasibility reassessment.
    carbonstack/roadmap/ROADMAP.md has been refreshed around v0.5.17.
    Local-backbone is closer and architecture-discussable, but not implementation-ready.
    No code was added in v0.5.17.
    No component repo changed in v0.5.17.
    No trust mutation was added in v0.5.17.
    No candidate storage was added in v0.5.17.
    No registry update was required.
    Validation passed.
    Final repo snapshot is clean and pushed.

Next safest action:

    v0.5.18 roadmap-refresh aftermath / implementation-priority decision.

Recommended v0.5.18 decision target:

    choose one narrow post-planning implementation or planning spike that reduces ambiguity without creating local-backbone yet.

Candidate directions:

    candidate identity draft/storage spike;
    mapped mismatch classifier spike;
    provider-event live-flow append integration spike;
    Relay Space join/invite/member planning;
    validation profile boundary planning;
    reset/recovery/re-enrollment planning.

Do not jump directly into:

    local-backbone profile;
    public deployment claims;
    Relay Space schema/API implementation;
    Relay Space join;
    broad candidate identity storage without schema decision;
    trust.json mutation from provider events;
    mapped mismatch mutation without tests and warning policy;
    provider identity import as verified trust;
    vault/PQ implementation;
    hostile-server claims;
    ack behavior changes;
    committing raw LogDoc/breakpoint files to Gitea.

The roadmap refresh is now complete for this planning arc. Future roadmap changes should be driven by concrete v0.5.18+ implementation-priority decisions, not by re-refreshing after every small rung.
